A novel architecture, c-siam, has been developed for classifying spoken language, utilizing a combination of contrastive and siamese models. By employing a contrastive model, c-siam extracts relevant features from speech data without the need for labels, and a siamese model is then utilized to identify linguistic patterns through paired utterances from a test example and a non-corresponding utterance from a database. c-siam's classification accuracy is enhanced by utilizing a gradient-descent-based loss function that minimizes the difference between the test example and its database counterpart. Furthermore, c-siam's effectiveness is demonstrated through its ability to classify spoken language in low-resource environments, achieving state-of-the-art results on the TIMIT database and comparable outcomes on the Librispeech dataset.

A new model for describing the interaction of neutrino-nucleon and neutrino-nucleus pairs has been developed. This model incorporates the results of recent measurements of the neutrino-nucleon total cross section and exclusive $p$ production to enhance its accuracy. Additionally, it includes the results of measurements of quasielastic and quasielastic-like charged-current neutrino-nucleus scattering. A comparison with previous versions of the model reveals significant improvements in the new model's ability to accurately predict neutrino-nucleus cross sections.

This research focuses on the almost-sure stabilization of an adaptive control system driven by a continuous-time hidden Markov chain. We establish a stabilization strategy that does not rely on prior knowledge of the system transition probabilities. Our method is based on the concept of dynamic programming for Markov decision processes with incomplete information.

This paper introduces the BTAI approach, a novel method for generating text-based input for video game state representations. In contrast to previous methods, such as Unibloc and Unicraft, which focus on specific game engines, BTAI offers a more universal and adaptable solution. The effectiveness of BTAI is demonstrated through comparisons with its predecessors, as well as a benchmark against the ProAI approach, resulting in notable enhancements in task completion speed and accuracy. The accompanying code for BTAI is available on the GitHub repository at https://github.com/BlueTaleAI/BlueTaleAI.

The Korteweg-de Vries equation's impact on the quark gluon plasma's behavior is examined, with a focus on its effect across different plasma states, including the hadron gas, quark gluon plasma, and stringy gas. The equation's connection to the plasma state is rooted in the hydrodynamic properties of the plasma, where the pressure and energy density drive the formation of a hydrodynamic scale, dictating the Lame coefficients in the Korteweg-de Vries equation. The influence of the equation of state on the plasma's behavior is significant, with variations in its strength affecting the amplitude of the plasma's long-wavelength perturbations.

We demonstrate in this note that the space of continuous functions on a compact set is linearly Eberlein-Grothendick if and only if it is completely metrizable. This is achieved by leveraging a recent discovery by M. Gruenbergs that the space of Radon measures on a compact set is Eberlein-Grothendick if and only if it is separable, along with the established fact that the space of Radon measures on a compact set is completely metrizable if and only to the space of continuous functions on that compact set is also metrizable.

We provide a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for an almost always
periodic Hamiltonian system to be isochronous on a two-dimensional
submanifold, terms of the Taylor series coefficients of the Hamiltonian 
function.

The global periodic orbit set for the Lorenz system is categorized based on its period lengths, with each period length denoted as $\mathcal{P}_n$. The study reveals that the open and closed flows of the Lorenz system are homeomorphic, with the same topological structure, denoted as $\mathcal{P}_0$. Additionally, it identifies that $\mathcal{P}_2$ is comprised of a saddle with a square cross-section, with its stable manifold intersecting the saddle's boundary at a single point, while $\mathcal{P}_3$ consists of a saddle with a triangle cross-section, with its stable manifold intersecting the saddle's boundary at a single point. The study further shows that $\mathcal{P}_1$ and $\mathcal{P}_2$ are topologically equivalent, with $\mathcal{P}_1$ containing a single point and $\mathcal{P}_2$ containing a single edge, while $\mathcal{P}_3$ is topologically equivalent to $\mathcal{P}_0$, with both containing a single vertex. The study also identifies that $\mathcal{P}_4$ and $\mathcal{P}_5$ are topologically equivalent to $\mathcal{P}_2$, with $\mathcal{P}_4$ containing two edges and $\mathcal{P}_5$ containing a square cross-section, with the same properties as $\mathcal{P}_2$.

In this research, we apply the Malliavin calculus to statistical models, 
yielding a direct link between Malliavin derivatives of log-likelihood and 
integrating operators on function spaces, thus bridging the gap between 
probability theory and functional analysis. Our findings enable the 
application of the Malliavin calculus to statistical inference, offering new 
insights. Specifically, we establish that the Malliavin basis functions can be 
used as a hierarchical expansion of a sample, leading to a novel method for 
obtaining maximum likelihood estimators based on Malliavin projections. 
Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Malliandin calculus can be employed to 
derive the asymptotic variances of maximum likelihood estimators without 
assuming asymptotic normality. Our results are substantiated through concrete 
examples, including the canonical logistic model, the ARMA model, and 
maximum likelihood estimation using the Malliavin basis.

We investigate the universal properties of the spectrum of Laplacians within vector bundles on curves, with respect to variations in the complex structure due to Teichmüller deformations. We demonstrate that as the representation of the fundamental group evolves, changes in the critical exponents of the representation are determined by the movement of eigenvalues in the $L^2$-spectrum of the Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish that the rate at which the $L^2$-spectrum shifts is, on average, directly proportional to the magnitude of the representation's deformation.

We introduce an autoregressive extension to the Fourier transform, demonstrating its suitability for predicting time-series data. The autoregressive Fourier coefficients of a time-series can be shown to form a low-dimensional, linear representation of that series. Utilizing this representation as input, we can generate synthetic data that closely resembles the original time-series, using a simple AR model. Furthermore, we propose a method for estimating the autoregressive Fourier coefficients of the time-series from its past values. Our experimental results confirm the effectiveness of this approach in predicting the autoregressive Fourier coefficients of a series based on its preceding values, resulting in significant improvements in predicting the original time-series.

We examine the connection between the cosmological constant and dark energy by analyzing how variations in the universe's fundamental energy density and the effective equation of state, known as w, impact the universe's mass function distribution. Utilizing the excursion set theory, we find that the predicted distribution of galaxy halos is highly dependent on the universe's energy density and the equation of state, and as such, it can be used to establish constraints on these parameters. Our analysis demonstrates that the predicted distribution is consistent with observations from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey, and the constraints we derive for the universe's energy density and the equation of state are consistent with current observational data and theoretical models.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing resource allocation for multi-access edge computing (MEC) systems through service function chaining (SFC). It presents a model that integrates resource allocation and routing decisions to minimize total service time for new flows in MEC systems with SFC. Due to its complexity, the model is broken down into two subproblems. The first subproblem involves finding the optimal set of MEC servers to allocate resources for each service function, while the second subproblem involves routing the flow through the assigned server resources. To solve this, a novel algorithm called Flow-aware Resource Allocation and Routing (FARR) is proposed, which utilizes a primal-dual subgradient method to solve the first subproblem and a dynamic programming algorithm to solve the second subproblem. FARR is shown to have a time complexity of O(NF^2), where N represents the number of MEC servers and NF represents the number of flow segments. Simulation results demonstrate that FARR outperforms the benchmark SFC-based algorithm by reducing total service time by up to 30%.

We investigate the impact of a random potential on a 2D Dirac fermion system with a topological gap in the presence of a constant magnetic field. Utilizing the functional renormalization group, we find that the disorder strength at which the fixed point is lost decreases as the coupling between the Dirac fermions and their environment increases. This result is supported by the findings of a recent numerical study.

This study examines the use of social media for those with depression and how it differs from the general population, focusing on both the negative and positive aspects of users' feeds. Our analysis reveals that individuals with depression tend to post fewer positive content regarding relationships, receive fewer replies, and post less frequently, with their positive content being less varied than the general population's. Moreover, the timing of their posts is less predictable, with their timelines containing fewer peaks and fewer consistent patterns. Our findings are consistent with prior research, indicating that those with depression exhibit similar patterns of reduced post frequency and fewer replies. However, our novel approach utilizing topic modeling shows that depressed individuals' positive content is less extensive than expected, suggesting potential utility in using social media data to identify depressed individuals prior to medical diagnosis.

A QCD-based theory with a lighter color charge can produce baryon-like composite particles that are heavy and stable, making them potential candidates for dark matter. The temperature-dependent mass variations in this scenario could provide a resolution to the small-scale problems in the standard dark matter model. A modified QCD theory with a lighter color charge can be achieved by introducing an additional interaction with the Higgs boson, which may also explain the observed dark matter density.

A comprehensive study of the Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$ single crystal was conducted using a combination of inductive and transport measurements, as well as X-ray diffraction and heat capacity analysis. The results of these measurements confirm that the compound exhibits a tetragonal structure with a nickel spin-1/2 property, and that the nickel moments are significantly reduced due to the effects of the crystalline electric field. The reduction in the nickel moments results in a significant decrease in the ferromagnetic transition temperature, and the presence of a spin gap in the low-temperature susceptibility data. The application of a magnetic field to the compound leads to a significant reduction in the transition temperature, and the development of a small magnetocaloric effect. The heat capacity data provide further evidence for the presence of a spin gap, and the presence of a small upturn at low temperatures, which is likely due to a type of magnetic ordering. The results of these measurements collectively demonstrate that the Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$ single crystal exhibits a type of magnetic ordering that is characterized by a spin-1/2 property, and the presence of a spin gap, and the presence of a small magnetocaloric effect.

The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the development of large-scale, distributed systems that rely heavily on collaboration between entities. Building trust is crucial in such systems, as it enables entities to make informed decisions about team composition and task delegation. However, the open and dynamic nature of IoT systems poses significant challenges to trust management, particularly in establishing trust between parties with no prior history or requiring continuous validation of trusted relationships. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of trust management solutions within IoT systems, focusing on the key objectives of trust establishment, maintenance, and transfer. It also explores the approaches used in IoT applications, such as edge computing, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and the 5G ecosystem. A detailed analysis of trust management solutions within these contexts is provided, along with a comprehensive review of trust evaluation methods. Finally, the paper identifies open challenges and areas for future research in trust management for IoT systems.

Cubic splines are commonly used in various applications, such as data analysis and curve fitting, due to their ability to provide a smooth approximation. However, the cubic spline method can lead to non-monotonic data when interpolating between points. This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing cubic splines that maintains data monotonicity while still producing a smooth approximation. The proposed method is further evaluated through numerical examples to demonstrate its superiority over existing monotone cubic spline methods.

We investigate the AdS/AdS and AdS/LaNY gravity duals for exact black bounce solutions in the AdS space, where we identify key differences in their phase structures compared to dS/dS and dS/LaNY scenarios. The study of energy density, pressure, and entropic force within these geometries reveals distinct features, including a unique 'hat' shape in entropic force in the AdS space that lacks the 'hump' observed in the dS case.

The growing interest in audio content has led to the exploration of automated methods for annotating audio, focusing on both segmentation and tagging. However, manual annotation of a vast range of audio content remains a laborious task due to its heterogeneity in length, genre, and tempo. To address this, we introduce a novel and efficient method that leverages automatic segmentation to streamline audio annotation. Our approach significantly reduces the number of frames requiring human annotation by up to 80%, as demonstrated through experiments on the MagnaTagClouds dataset. Additionally, we showcase the potential of our system through a user interface demonstration.

The relationship between species abundance fluctuations and ecological stability is crucial in understanding biodiversity stability. We investigate this relationship in complex networks, specifically in models where species interact through positive and negative influences, and find that local fluctuations in abundance determine long-term stability globally. Moreover, our analysis reveals that the magnitude of fluctuations in these models depends on the interaction patterns within the network, and we have identified a quantitative measure that can predict this dependence based on the distribution of connections.

We examine the progression of network avalanches triggered by the sequential removal of nodes, where each step involves the immediate removal of adjacent nodes whose connections have been disrupted. Our analysis reveals that the intensity of these avalanches exhibits a power-law distribution. We demonstrate how the overall size of an avalanche correlates with the size of the initial node it's built upon, as well as the varying thresholds for activation and final fragmentation. Furthermore, we identify a novel critical dimension for percolation in the context of networks, which depends on the degree distribution of the nodes. Our findings also indicate that the progression of avalanches in scale-free networks like the Barabási-Albert model is influenced by the same critical dimension as those in regular lattices.

Despite the substantial progress made in NLP, creating models capable of comprehensive discourse understanding across complex texts remains an unresolved challenge. A significant hurdle lies in the absence of a universally accepted framework for discourse structure, making it difficult to develop structured representations. To address this, we introduce a novel, unsupervised approach for generating structured representations of complex texts. This method leverages the attention mechanism to dynamically identify the most relevant spans and span boundaries. By optimizing the attention matrix through dynamic programming, we ensure that the span boundaries conform to specific tree shapes. Experimental results on two prominent tree construction datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our approach.

Seismic wave simulations, a core component of seismology, are often tackled using the finite-difference (FD) method, but this approach is limited by its high computational costs. To overcome this challenge, researchers have turned to the finite-element method, but this method's accuracy relies heavily on the mesh's coarseness, making it difficult to achieve precise results without excessive computational resources. In contrast, the spectral finite-element method offers superior accuracy at a significantly lower computational cost. Although it has been successfully applied to various geophysics problems, the FEM has traditionally been reserved for smaller-scale issues due to its high implementation complexity. In this study, we introduce a novel spectral element method that can be integrated with the finite-element framework, allowing us to achieve the same level of accuracy as the spectral finite-element method at a lower cost. Our proposed approach is demonstrated on a range of seismological problems, including 2D and 3D wave propagation, source-receiver interactions, and 2D gravity inversion, yielding results that are comparable to or even surpassing those of the spectral finite-element method.

The dynamic behavior of two interacting droplets can be analyzed through a droplet model, which involves the study of a two-dimensional complex-valued partial differential equation. A particular butterfly-like breakup has been identified in the droplet interactions, occurring when the initial radius of one droplet is above a specific threshold and the initial radius of the other is above a different threshold determined by the first. As these minimum radii are achieved in the course of the droplet merging, the breakup of the other droplet is observed. A new instability mechanism has been proposed to explain this phenomenon, which involves the interaction between the radial and transverse modes of the droplet.

The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) is generating immense amounts of data, which is challenging the existing network infrastructure. To address this, advanced traffic management techniques are required. To this end, we suggest employing Software-Defined Networking (SDN) to optimize data traffic management. SDN enables the precise control of network traffic by allowing the placement of IoT devices in specific locations. However, the limited availability of IoT devices in key locations often results in suboptimal traffic paths. To address this, we propose a novel algorithm that uses a graph-based model to place IoT devices and minimize traffic paths. Our evaluation of this approach using real-world network data and traffic patterns demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing average traffic distances by up to 35.5%.

The formation of planets and the surrounding protoplanetary disk are intricately linked. The presence of a planet within a disk causes a complex interaction that alters the disk's structure and the motion of surrounding particles. The study of how the disk and the planet influence each other is crucial in understanding planetary formation. The research presented here focuses on a specific type of disk model that takes into account the effects of a planet's gravitational field on the surrounding particles. The study also investigates how the planet's orbital path influences the disk's shape and the distribution of particles within it. By simulating the long-term behavior of particles in the disk, researchers can gain insights into the planet's presence and the disk's evolution. The study also examines how the planet's gravitational influence affects the distribution of particles in the disk, and how this can be observed from the sky. The results of the study are compared with real observations of protoplanetary disks to infer the presence of the planet. The study demonstrates that the planet's effects on the disk can be observed and used to infer its presence and orbital path. The study also presents a new method for analyzing observations of protoplanetary disks to infer the presence of the planet.

Geometric models based on Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces have gained significant attention in representation learning, particularly in the analysis of geometric structures and their practical applications. However, these models often rely on simplified assumptions that do not accurately represent the complexities of real-world data. In contrast, geometric models based on symmetric positive definite matrices have been found to be more robust in practice, despite their less favorable geometric structure. In this study, we investigate the relationship between these two types of geometric models and demonstrate that the latter can be viewed as a specific instance of the former, thus bridging the gap between the two.

The study examines the feasibility of hydrogen transportation from the US western region to the Eastern seaborne terminals via existing pipeline infrastructure. It demonstrates that approximately 70% of the required hydrogen backbone can be assembled by repurposing existing pipeline systems, with the remainder constructed from scratch. A pipeline refurbishment cost of $50,000 per mile results in a total investment of $10 billion to form the hydrogen backbone. A network optimization model is utilized to determine optimal pipeline capacities, with results indicating a capacity of 1.5 million standard cubic feet per day for most pipeline sections. With 1,000 nodes, the model's solution time is approximately 10 minutes. A comparative analysis of the investment required for the hydrogen backbone using the existing pipeline infrastructure versus a grid-like structure shows that the former necessitates significantly less investment - a difference of $10 billion.

A study of the sun using data from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory revealed a connection between the magnetic fields beneath and on the sun's surface. Researchers found that when comparing the direction of these magnetic fields, the difference between the two is relatively small, just 5.6 degrees. This outcome is significantly lower than what was predicted by a theoretical model and suggests that convective motion within the sun is not as turbulent as previously thought.

In recent years, significant advancements have been made in producing squeezed states of light within integrated optics.  A notable breakthrough in this field has been achieved through the use of topological phases, which have led to the development of various devices such as photonic lattices and crystal-based waveguides.  This research has primarily focused on the generation of squeezed photon currents, but a new study demonstrates the potential for topological phases to produce genuine squeezed vacuum states of light within integrated circuits.  A proof-of-concept device has been proposed, which utilizes a combination of photonic crystals and a nonlinear material to create such states.  The device's performance has been simulated using finite-difference time-domain methods, which have shown that it can efficiently produce high-quality squeezed states of light.  This advancement in integrated optics is expected to pave the way for the development of new photonic devices that can harness the unique properties of topological phases to create novel quantum states of light.

This research introduces a novel trajectory planning algorithm for drones that surpasses the performance of polynomial trajectory methods by significantly reducing total travel time. The new approach generates an optimal path for the drone by first dividing it into segments and applying a linear acceleration planning strategy to each segment. A recursive optimization process then determines the number and locations of the segments, ensuring minimal overall travel time. Unlike existing methods, this approach doesn't impose pre-determined limits on the number of segments and is therefore more effective in navigating complex environments. Furthermore, the algorithm can be easily modified to accommodate multiple drones. Experimental results using actual drone platforms demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in outperforming polynomial planning by up to 25%.
An enumeration of F_q-invariant linear additive conjugacy codes of a specified length is presented along with an analysis of their distribution.

The unfulfilled potential of the 2020 online workshop on Alumni Engagement for HEP Researchers has motivated us to create a more detailed plan for incorporating such initiatives into the DESY Physics Program. This initiative aims to support the development of skills that facilitate physicists' transition from academic careers to industry positions.

The W boson polarization can be determined from the angle between the top quark's b-quark and the direct W boson product decay. The analysis utilizes a sample of t-bar t events at the LHC, specifically utilizing a sample of 2.2 inverse femtobarns of data collected with the CMS detector. The chosen observable is independent of production details and is influenced by the W boson's polarization state. The analysis utilizes a multivariate approach to boost the signal-to-background ratio, resulting in a background estimate of 0.025 and a signal value of 1.04. The analysis yields a statistical accuracy of 0.16 and an absolute W boson polarization determination of 0.15 with a 68% confidence level.

New sum rules for the ξ-moments of D-meson distribution amplitudes are derived using light-cone QCD sum rules. These additional rules enhance the available sum rules from the literature, leading to more information about the shape functions. Specifically, a relation involving ξ3 and ξ4 provides valuable insight into the third power of the light-cone distribution amplitude f3, which is challenging to study experimentally. By analyzing the ratio of ξ3 to ξ4, it is possible to determine the value of the strong coupling constant at the scale of the heavy quark mass.

In power graph theory, researchers have thoroughly studied eigenvalue problems for undirected graphs. However, in the case of directed graphs, there has been a lack of comprehensive research on the eigenvalues of power directed graphs. This study addresses this gap by developing a theoretical framework for directed power graphs. By establishing a connection between the eigenvalues of directed power hypergraphs and the number of signed subgraphs, we provide a clear, direct relationship between these concepts. This connection enables us to derive a formula for the eigenvalues of directed power hypergraphs and, subsequently, of directed power graphs. The results obtained in this research can be applied to develop a new approach to eigenvalue computation for various types of directed power graphs.

This study introduces a novel method for determining the position and velocity of a satellite by using measurements between satellites. By utilizing the average position of multiple inter-satellite measurements, the proposed inter-satellite network can achieve a location accuracy comparable to a combination of inter-satellite and ground station data. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that inter-satellite networks can be scaled up by adding more satellites without compromising accuracy, as long as their orbits remain operational.

The exoplanet XO-3b, a hot Jupiter, has been observed to have an unusually short orbital period that is rapidly decreasing, with this decrease becoming more pronounced over the years. This phenomenon is thought to be caused by the strong tidal forces exerted by the star on the planet, and recent observations have revealed a more significant rate of decrease than initially anticipated. This article presents the findings of 22 days of photometric monitoring of the star XO-3 with the 2.4m telescope at La Silla Observatory, with a cadence of 1 minute. The data collected in 2014 and 2015 showed that the decrease in the planet's orbital period has accelerated, with a more precise measurement of this acceleration than previous studies. This acceleration is thought to be the result of the star's gravitational pull on the planet, and the data collected in 2015 provides a more precise measurement of this effect than previous studies.

The calibration of complex astrophysical experiments is a crucial aspect of producing reliable measurements. This process involves using a reference dataset to adjust the scale and offset of measurements, but its uncertainty is often overlooked. To address this gap, we have developed a Bayesian approach combined with machine learning to automatically calculate the uncertainties associated with calibration. By implementing this method in a real-world scenario using the MeerKAT radio telescope as an example, we have obtained robust uncertainty estimates. We believe this approach can be adapted to other experiments in astrophysics and serve as a foundation for further advancements, such as improved calibration algorithms and new machine learning techniques.

We establish a relationship between the genus zero equivariant Gromov-Witten theory of projective bundles and the invariants of their underlying vector bundles. This connection enables us to reframe the Witten-Donaldson theorem's determination of quantum cohomology for symplectic manifolds through vector bundles, making it applicable to projective bundles. Furthermore, our findings yield new insights into the structure of the equivariant Gromov-Witten theory of projective bundles, including key properties such as Witten's theorem and the Buryak's hypergeometric identity.

We establish a functional equation for the Rankin-Selberg L-function in the context of an arbitrary automorphic representation on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over a rational number field, specifically focusing on cases where the representation is not necessarily cuspidal. We also derive finite places contributions. Our proof relies on the classical inverse trace formula and the central identity from the arithmetic Jacquet-Langlands correspondence.

In clinical trials, researchers often focus on continuous outcomes, yet conventional statistical models frequently overlook the limitations imposed by the constraints of experimental designs. A novel approach is introduced to analyze data that are bounded by specific limits, employing natural cubic spline functions to approximate the underlying distribution. By leveraging these spline functions, an adaptive estimation method is developed to adjust for the constraints, leading to more accurate estimates. The performance of this method is evaluated through both simulated and actual data from the BIRT trial, demonstrating its superiority over traditional models in terms of consistency and reduced bias. Additionally, this analysis showcases the application of the proposed approach to examine the relationship between certain biomarkers and clinical outcomes.

Our proposed routing algorithm, CRAWLING, utilizes a continuous-time Markov chain to model state transitions and accurately reflect the time it takes for control planes to exchange packets and run routing protocols. This allows CRAWLING to account for the fact that control planes are not instantaneous, but instead operate on a millisecond timescale, in contrast to the typically assumed deterministic and delay-free approach in existing work.

A long-standing debate in machine learning is whether flat-minima optimization is beneficial or not. To resolve this controversy, we conducted an in-depth analysis of two prominent scaling techniques: weight clipping and spectral normalization. We compared their effects on the generalization error of fully-connected networks and found that they behave similarly in terms of generalization error, but have distinct scaling mechanisms. We also discovered that the two methods can be combined to achieve better generalization performance. However, this improvement comes at the cost of requiring more complex scaling parameters. Our results suggest that flat-minima optimization is not inherently superior and that different scaling techniques have varying levels of effectiveness.

A parametric FSL with low insertion loss and high power threshold was created
using an X-Band magnetron, enabling reliable protection of receivers from strong
power overload. This device effectively reduces high power above a specific
threshold by attenuating it below a minimum level, ensuring the signal remains
stable below this threshold. As a result, the signal is effectively managed, and
the limiter provides consistent output power within the operating range. Notably,
the FSL exhibits low insertion loss and an impressive power threshold, demonstrating
its potential as a cost-effective and efficient device for a wide range of
applications.

We examine the effect of controlling an epidemic with quarantines, using a model that accounts for the social and economic impact of these measures. Our analysis reveals that the model can produce stable equilibria where the disease is eliminated, and that the use of quarantine can delay this outcome. However, this benefit comes at a significant cost due to the social and economic effects of these measures. Our research also shows that the model can produce multiple solutions where the disease is eliminated, and that the use of quarantine can alter the trajectory of the epidemic. Specifically, introducing or relaxing quarantine measures can amplify, dampen or have no effect on subsequent waves of the epidemic.

We investigated the value of incorporating context information from sentence alignment and structural features from dependency trees in supervised term matching. Our findings indicate that combining sentence context and structural features leads to improved matching performance compared to using only structural features. Notably, incorporating context from sentence alignment substantially enhances matching performance when using structural features.

We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the cluster at the origin in a d-dimensional Poisson Boolean model with expanding Euclidean balls as its clusters, and analyze how the probability of such a cluster grows or decreases relative to the Poisson cluster process as the number of clusters increases.

This study utilizes three-dimensional simulations of rotating convective-dense shell stellar material to model the emergence of a baroclinically unstable region. We've developed a method to generate equilibrium states for our simulations, which draws on rapidly rotating toroidal flows. We've found that these equilibrium states effectively capture the complex dynamics involved in the development of a self-gravitating system. By applying conservation of angular momentum, we've derived a system of equations that allows us to model the equilibrium states. We've then used these equilibrium states as initial conditions for our three-dimensional simulations, which have successfully reproduced the development of a baroclinically unstable region.

The Lema\^{\i}tre-Tolman-Bondi model has been expanded upon by introducing a new variable, the structure scalar, to aid in understanding its structure. A related metric was proposed, the generalized Lema\^{\i}tre-Tolman-Bondi spacetime, with a variable density profile. The structure scalars were calculated for this new metric and found to exhibit distinct behavior compared to the standard model, with a notable effect on the structure function. The calculated scalars were then compared to the mass model, with a notable finding that the structure scalar was dependent on the metric's variable density profile.

In quantum theory, nonlocality is a significant phenomenon that surpasses the capabilities of classical physics, particularly in multi-party systems. Our research demonstrates that nonlocal behavior becomes apparent when attempting to conceal correlations between multiple parties using local methods. We have identified a hidden nonlocality principle that applies to all multipartite systems, and its minimum manifestation is measured in the context of local hiding capacity. Our findings are supported by the analysis of various quantum states, including the three-qubit GHZ state, and its generalizations, as well as the N-qubit W state. Our research also reveals that nonlocal sets of local hiding channels can be created through the application of local operations and communications.

This study introduces a novel approach to predicting visual attention regions
on web pages by leveraging multilabel classification techniques. A comprehensive
dataset comprising 1,185 web page images, 14 labels, and relevant description
tags was developed. To accurately identify relevant areas of focus, we employed
multilabel classification methods and a range of loss functions. Our proposed
methodology was then applied to isolate areas of interest from the predicted
labels, and the results were manually evaluated for accuracy. Experimental
findings demonstrated the efficacy of our approach, which outperformed existing
methods in accurately capturing web users' visual attention regions in web
browsing scenarios.

A novel 2-bit transmissive RIS element is introduced, offering enhanced phase modulation capabilities compared to existing solutions. The proposed RIS element utilizes a combination of transmission and phase shifting in its 2-bit format, allowing for a greater phase range of $\pi$ compared to the standard $\pi$-phase RIS. The transmissive nature of the RIS element is achieved through a wedge-like design that enables efficient energy transmission. The RIS element's performance is demonstrated through simulations of communication and sensing applications. The results show that the transmissive RIS element can improve communication link reliability and sensing system accuracy.

We've developed a novel approach to efficient offline reinforcement learning, 
which involves converting the RL problem into a linear-programming form to 
enable the utilization of efficient algorithms from the online LP 
counterfactual decomposition framework. This technique allows for policy 
parameterization and efficient computation, thereby enabling the derivation of 
low-regret policies in a high-quality way. We've successfully adapted this 
method to address a variety of offline LP settings, including contextual LP 
regret minimization, unsupervised behavior cloning, and supervised learning. 
Additionally, we've established sample efficiency bounds for our proposed 
algorithms and have tested them in both synthetic and real-world scenarios.

In this paper, we explore a broader interpretation of higher inductive types within homotopy type type theory, allowing them to encompass not just the fundamental groups but also the higher-dimensional homotopy groups of various spaces. We establish a specific framework that enables us to study the homotopy groups of spaces through type theory, including a method for generating these types and an analysis of the weak equivalence concept. Furthermore, we examine the connection between homotopy groups of a space and their corresponding loop types, providing a detailed analysis of the impact of the loop types on the space's homotopy groups.

This compact object is situated within a 740 million solar mass galaxy, displaying a peculiar structure. Notably, the black hole resides 0.5 kiloparsecs from its expected location, aligning with a past galaxy collision event. This anomaly is thought to be a result of the galaxy merger that occurred 0.5-1.5 billion years ago. This event led to the formation of a unique structure known as a galaxy collision event. In a recent study, researchers have thoroughly examined the existence of periodic solutions in the three-body problem where the masses are distinct and vary in a specific range. Building upon this research, a new analysis has been conducted to explore the existence of periodic solutions where the masses are not only unique but also vary over a broader range. This investigation has led to the discovery of novel open and closed periods of motion, characterized by novel configurations of closed and open periods. Crucially, these new findings have been shown to include previously identified open periods of motion, thereby providing a more comprehensive understanding of the problem.

A novel approach to fluorescence imaging utilizes the spatial interference patterns formed when multiple fluorescent objects emit light within the same diffraction lens' focal plane. By analyzing the interference patterns created by light from these objects, it's possible to reconstruct the spatial distribution of the fluorescent objects. However, this method relies on a simplified model that assumes light travels in straight lines, which isn't entirely accurate. In this study, we investigate the accuracy of this method when light behaves in a more complex manner, specifically when light is scattered by a diffuse layer. We found that while this method still yields useful results, it's more sensitive to scattering in this case compared to straight-line propagation.

User preference modeling is a critical task in recommendation systems. Although recent research has made significant progress in modeling user behavior patterns, there is still a gap in understanding how local (item-level) and global (session-level or user-level) patterns interact with each other. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that incorporates both patterns into a unified representation. Our approach, called Local-Global User Behavior Modeling (LGUBM), leverages item transitions to capture local patterns and session embeddings to capture global patterns. We demonstrate that combining these patterns leads to improved performance, surpassing existing baselines in click-through rate prediction on public datasets.

The use of Euclidean distances in graph embedding is a well-established approach, yet geodesic similarity can offer a more comprehensive graph representation learning method due to its ability to capture complex network structures. This study introduces a novel graph embedding framework that leverages geodesic similarity, which we demonstrate can accurately infer graph nodes without relying on supervision signals. Furthermore, we prove the proposed method's potential to learn node representations even in undirected graphs and identify key characteristics of the resulting representations. Additionally, we provide an efficient optimization technique for large-scale graph inference, which we validate by achieving superior performance compared to conventional supervised learning methods across multiple graph types.

This research investigates the uplink grant-free access in massive MIMO systems, utilizing non-orthogonal sequences to enable simultaneous transmission by multiple users. The proposed sequence design optimizes the minimum distance between the sequences to facilitate efficient maximum likelihood detection, thereby reducing the performance gap compared to orthogonal sequences. The study also evaluates the performance of ML detection and ZF methods, considering the impact of user interactions and random sequence ordering.

We introduce a novel factorization approach, called Decoder-Expander Based Factorisation (DEBF), which builds on the principles of Decoder-Expander Coding. This method is designed to efficiently reconstruct sparse codes from a linear number of observations, leveraging the built-in sparsity of the code to produce a more accurate and efficient solution. Furthermore, DEBF factorises the observation matrix into smaller sub-matrices, enabling separate low-complexity reconstructions of the recovered codes. Our analysis shows that DEBF achieves near-optimal reconstruction success probability with linear time complexity, under the same conditions as optimal decoder for the linear measurement model. Simulation results confirm the superior performance of DEBF in terms of decoding accuracy and speed, making it a promising alternative to traditional compressed sensing methods.

This study introduces a novel approach to data augmentation, utilizing differentiable adversarial spatial transformers to create tailored transformations for each image. By mapping each pixel to a low-dimensional space, our method identifies and removes the inherent style of the original images, thereby yielding more diverse and realistic transformations. As a result, our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of diversity and the discriminatory power of classification models, without the need for additional hyperparameter optimization. We also explore the potential of our style-preserving data augmentation in segmentation tasks and examine its utility as a defense mechanism against adversarial attacks.

We investigate spatial derivatives operating on self-adjoint map algebra with infinite dimension and dimensionality. It's found that 2-local spatial derivatives within infinite dimensional map algebra with self-adjoint matrix values are represented by unbounded operators. These operators, when acting on specific map algebra with self-adjoint matrix values, are bounded. Moreover, we've identified the adjoints of these operators, their physical meanings, and we've also explored the physical applications of 2-local spatial derivatives within map algebra with self-adjoint matrix values.

The topological characteristics of Berry's phase are investigated for a four-level system under the influence of time-dependent and varying fields. The dynamics in the parameter space around a level crossing leads to the formation of a complex Berry phase topology with toroidal and spherical shapes. The results demonstrate a dependence on the duration of the pulse sequences and the strength of the varying field. The findings are significant for the field of quantum optics research.

In BECs with spin-orbit coupling, our study reveals the existence of compactons, which are localized compactons, by examining the stability of a specific configuration using a variational approach. This compacton configuration is stable when certain conditions are met, specifically when the ratio of $\lambda$ to $\kappa$ is greater than or equal to 1 and the ratio of $\lambda$ to $2\kappa$ is greater than or equal to $3 \sqrt{2}$. Furthermore, our results show that the compacton's length scales with the parameter $\lambda$ and exhibits a similar behavior to a Gaussian envelope.

The heavy quark limit's effect on the decay width ratios of certain b to u decays is examined, specifically for the transitions t to u versus b to d decays. By using the results from lattice QCD, it's demonstrated that the ratios involving the vector matrix element approach unity, yet substantial disparities arise when considering the ratios involving the axial-vector and scalar matrix elements from those predicted by the heavy quark symmetry due to strong finite box size effects.

Consider a smooth manifold M with an action of a Lie group G that acts smoothly and effectively on M. This work focuses on the orbit space $\Omega_G(M)$ resulting from G's action on M, where net function approximation properties are examined. The properties of the orbit space under different types of G actions on M are investigated, including those that are free, proper, or linear. The work also analyzes the topological and metric properties of the orbit space, particularly in relation to G's structure and the properties of M, and provides a comprehensive description of the various possible topologies on G. Furthermore, it is shown that certain topologies on G can be induced from the orbit space, and demonstrate how specific classes of functions on G can be approximated on G by continuous functions on M.

A future muon collider could significantly enhance the search for heavy axion-like particles (ALPs) at a single, high-energy hadron collider, particularly through the examination of lepton pairs in specific final states. By utilizing the fact that ALPs can convert into photons and decaying photons into lepton-phonon pairs, a muon collider can provide a comprehensive understanding of ALP production, allowing researchers to investigate the phenomenon across a broad mass range, from a few MeV to multiple TeV. The addition of a muon collider's data would provide crucial information about ALP interactions with hadrons and thus complement existing and future LHC searches.

To accelerate the adoption of new ideas in hardware, we present MetaSys, an open-source, extensible framework that allows researchers to seamlessly integrate, test, and compare various hardware techniques using a standardized, high-performance testbench. MetaSys is a versatile, language-agnostic platform that enables the rapid creation of system prototypes and evaluation tools. Its modular design consists of three key components: a meta-synthesizable core, a testbench, and a suite of tools for analysis, testing, and comparison. With MetaSys, developers can efficiently build, simulate, and optimize hardware systems, including processors, accelerators, and interconnects. Our framework is implemented in Verilog and optimized for the SPARC T4 processor, but it can be easily adapted to other platforms. MetaSys is now available under an open-source license, including its source code, documentation, and online tools, at https://sites.google.com/a/paessler.com/metasys/home/.

In recent years, the field of biotechnology has seen significant advancements in the development of biologic medicines, but their production is often hindered by significant operational inefficiencies. To address this issue, we propose a Twin-VAE framework that utilizes a combination of variational autoencoders to create a more efficient transfer learning approach for predicting critical process performance variables. By leveraging a single, easily accessible dataset from a development context, we can train our model to simultaneously learn both data manifold structures and relationships between input variables and key outcomes. Our approach was tested on a large-scale CHO-K1 suspension growth dataset, and we found that it significantly outperformed traditional transfer learning methods. Notably, our model was able to achieve a 20% reduction in mean absolute error for key outcomes when trained on a smaller development dataset and tested on a large-scale production dataset.

We introduce an innovative method for proving the density of weak solutions in a differential equation that transforms them into strong solutions. Our approach is applied to the Cauchy problem for the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with electronic gap, providing a simple proof of the existence of a strong solution in the energy space. Crucially, this strong solution adheres to the initial conditions with exactness.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have led to the widespread adoption of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for modeling sequential data. Despite their success, RNNs often struggle with the long-term dependencies in complex datasets. To address this challenge, we propose a novel architecture, the Fourier Recurrent Unit (FRU), which leverages the Fourier basis to improve gradient flow and information sharing between different parts of the sequence. By integrating a Fourier matrix into the RNN, FRU enables the network to focus on specific frequency components of the input sequence. Our experiments on various datasets show that FRU outperforms traditional RNNs and LSTMs, and sensitivity analysis reveals that the Fourier matrix's parameters play a crucial role in capturing the underlying data patterns.

This paper investigates the problem of actively identifying a subset of $k$ items in a set of $N$ items with minimal interaction, extending the concept of active PAC learning introduced by Dasgupta et al. in 2019, which applies to classification tasks. The generative setting involves learning from a target function's random examples drawn from a known distribution, whereas the online setting involves sequential access to a target function's examples. The paper demonstrates that these two settings have different difficulty levels, with the generative setting being significantly more challenging. Specifically, it shows that any algorithm addressing the generative setting must use $\Omega(K\log(N/K))$ queries to achieve a certain level of accuracy, whereas a simpler algorithm using $\Theta(K\log(N/K))$ queries can address the online setting with ease. The paper also presents an algorithm that matches the lower bound for the generative setting under certain conditions.

The process of relativistic laser-matter interaction in a solid jet produces attosecond electrons with unique properties, including a specific direction of spin. This spin influences how these electrons behave in a plasma wake, leading to distinct characteristics in the generated sideband electron beams. By analyzing the spin dynamics, researchers can control the trajectory and focus of these beams. This capability allows for the development of novel instruments to study the interaction between high-energy particles and matter at the sub-femtosecond scale.

This paper explores the dynamics of vital field driven transformations within the framework of non-equilibrium thermodynamics, particularly focusing on the thermodynamic properties of mutations that occur through the vital field. As mutations driven by the vital field deviate from classical mutations, we delve into the associated changes in entropy and reveal that they can be described as Brownian motions governed by the dynamics of key parameters. Furthermore, we establish a connection between the vital field and the rate of mutation by demonstrating that the probability density function of the mutation rate is linked to the potential energy of the system.

The growing need for interconnected Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) ecosystems worldwide is reflected in a multitude of local and regional initiatives. The diverse range of systems, tools, and formats used to track and analyze the interactions within these ecosystems results in isolated data sources. Achieving interoperability among these sources is crucial to gain a comprehensive understanding of the broader ecosystem. This paper introduces the Conceptual System for Interoperability (CSI), which is demonstrated through the implementation of the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG), an infrastructure that enables the creation of machine-readable, interlinked research objects. By facilitating the integration of various data sources, ORKG contributes to a unified understanding of the research landscape, offering new perspectives on research outputs, collaborations, and credit distribution within the ecosystem.

Android NDK functions are frequently used in Android applications but lack the robust side-channel protection mechanisms found in Java functions. As a result, Android NDK functions are often susceptible to side-channel leaks, putting user privacy at risk. To address this vulnerability, we developed LibALCHEM, a library that enables developers to fortify Android NDK functions against side-channels. Based on LibALCHEM, we created two concrete implementations, LibALCHEM-JNI and LibALCHEM-C++ and -Java, to enhance Android applications and native Android NDK functions, respectively. Our comprehensive testing and evaluation of LibALCHEM revealed that it effectively protects Android applications and native Android NDK functions from side-channel leaks.

Ego networks based on Ethereum's core transactions have become a valuable tool in studying self-interest versus collective well-being. Implementing temporal analysis into these networks has the potential to uncover hidden patterns in ego-centric community dynamics. We propose a method to extract and analyze the temporal properties of ego networks derived from the Ethereum blockchain, which leverages a self-attention based neural network to capture the temporal evolution of these communities. Our results demonstrate that this approach can identify distinct phases within Ethereum's growth, as well as predict the number of transactions in upcoming periods, all while outperforming existing methods in both predictions and understandings of community structure.

The LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ (LAO/STO) interface, a heterostructure of great interest,
exhibits extraordinary electronic and magnetic properties, especially when
subject to optical illumination. This phenomenon is attributed to the creation of
mobile charge carriers, whose impact on the magnetotransport properties is
significant. To investigate this effect, we utilized a unique device that allows
for the separation of the transport properties at the interface from those of
surrounding materials. Our study reveals that photo-illuminated LAO/STO interfaces
display a variety of anomalous magnetotransport behaviors, including a notable
insulator-to-metal transition, which is highly sensitive to the applied magnetic
field. This unusual phenomenon is thought to be the result of the interaction between
the generated mobile charge carriers and the persistent charge carriers, whose
movement is restricted by the interface potential.

A category of lattice-valued algebras has been developed to provide a framework for non-deterministic classical proof theory. The study of algebraic structures such as lattice-valued logics, including their corresponding deduction algebras, has been ongoing for some time. The focus of this paper is on pomset logic, a particular deduction algebraic structure. The paper demonstrates that the provability in pomset logic is more computationally intensive than in another logic, BV, but less so than in a more complex structure known as the Lambek calculus with cancellative sequents. The paper also establishes a relationship between pomset logic and linear logic by showing that a fragment of pomset logic aligns with a particular linear logic system.

Building on Mellit's work, a Macdonald polynomial version of the five-term relation has been discovered by Garsia and Mellit. This relation can be generalized to the context of non-graded ring t, and the resulting generalization leads to a new set of polynomials in t, known as the generalized Macdonald polynomials. This new family of polynomials is shown to include a special case of the Hall-Littlewood polynomials and can also be used to derive a t-analogue of the Weyl formula for classical groups.

The availability of spectroscopic redshifts is crucial for developing and training machine learning models for photometric redshifts. This paper presents the creation of a large photometric dataset, derived from 20,000 galaxy images from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, and is used to investigate the performance of models in redshifts beyond 0.6. A model was trained using a deep convolutional neural network and a U-Net architecture, and its performance was evaluated by comparing the resulting predictions with actual spectroscopic redshifts. The dataset was generated using the Tractor algorithm, simulating galaxy positions, shapes, photometry, and other properties. The training process involved randomly selecting galaxies from the dataset, and then using the Tractor algorithm to generate new images with the same galaxy properties. The resulting images were used to train a deep convolutional neural network, and a U-Net model was trained using these images. The models were then trained and tested using the same dataset, and their performance was evaluated by comparing the resulting predictions with actual spectroscopic redshifts. The results show that the models achieved an accuracy of 0.95 in redshifts beyond 0.6, and 0.97 in redshifts beyond 0.8. This paper presents a Bayesian decision support system to assess the operational costs of various policy options for a specific route operated by Dublin Bus. The system combines data from a point-based travel survey and smart card data to analyze fuel consumption and traffic congestion. By utilizing Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations, the system's parameters are calibrated and multiple scenarios are evaluated. Ultimately, the system provides an analysis of the effects different policies have on Dublin Bus' costs and offers an estimate of the uncertainty associated with these effects.

We have developed a method to exactly recover the FCI energy in a two-electron system using a QC-DMRG approach in a continuous space. In this approach, we use an auxiliary variable to represent the coefficient of a two-body operator, which allows us to exactly recover the FCI energy with a 2-RVB. However, this approach leads to a non-hermitian Hamiltonian matrix, making it difficult to recover the FCI energy using the same algorithm. Therefore, we have also developed a method to exactly diagonalize this non-hermitian matrix, which involves a simple transformation to a hermitian matrix using the operator norm. Our results show that this approach can recover the FCI energy with high accuracy, even with a small number of states.

We investigate a scenario in which a dark matter particle arises from a dark sector consisting of two Higgs bosons. The dark sector's interactions with the Standard Model are facilitated through kinetic mixing between $Z$ and Higgs bosons and photon and Higgs boson interactions. The kinetic mixing is a result of a tree-level coupling, while the Higgs boson interactions are a result of a dark sector pion's one-loop interaction. The dark matter's relic abundance is determined by its tree-level interaction with the dark pion. The muon's anomalous magnetic moment is addressed through a tree-level coupling between the dark matter and a photon mediated by a dark pion. The dark matter's mass is constrained to be in the range of 2-10 GeV. The direct detection experiments' bounds on dark matter interactions are applied to further restrict the dark matter mass. The dark matter's detection prospects in future direct search experiments are also analyzed.

A groundbreaking approach to simulation has been developed by combining the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) with the PyECM code, enabling the prediction of complex coastal flooding dynamics. By leveraging FNO's efficiency, the proposed method accelerates the computation time by 3-4 times without compromising accuracy, resulting in highly detailed 6h time steps for high-resolution simulations covering extensive areas. The integration of FNO with PyECM was made possible through a novel data processing technique, which prepares the input for the neural network by combining and reformulating the boundary conditions of the hydrodynamic model. The proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness by successfully simulating the flooding dynamics in San Francisco, achieving notable improvements in both accuracy and computational efficiency. The results show that the model is capable of simulating the full tidal cycle with a high degree of accuracy, resulting in highly detailed and realistic simulations.

A joint analysis platform called CAMSpec3, built by the Cosmology And Astrophysics Mapping Society, offers a comprehensive analysis tool for the CMB. Through partnerships with various CMB projects, this software is community-driven and free for use by anyone. In this document, we outline the creation of CAMSpec3, discuss its connection to previous versions, and explain each component's functionality. CAMSpec3 is accessible online through the link camspec3.readthedocs.org.

Our research focuses on the diffusion of activators and inhibitors across the interconnected nodes of a complex network, utilizing a mean-field approximation to derive a set of simplified equations. Through these equations, we examine the conditions that lead to the emergence of Turing instability, taking into account the varying degrees of diffusion between and within different network compartments. Our findings indicate that the diffusion rates of activators and inhibitors have distinct influences on the conditions for Turing instability, with significant effects observed when the slower species diffuses more freely across network compartments than the faster species.

We investigate the impact of a phantom field on a $\phi^4$ theory, demonstrating that it breaks the conservation of an induced supercurrent, and thus, cannot be equivalent to a conventional supersymmetric theory. Our findings are consistent with the concept that an extra component is necessary for ultraviolet completion in the Standard Model, as proposed by Andersen et al. in 2017.

The electronic properties of core/shell GaAs/AlGaAs nanowires were studied using angle-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy at low temperatures. The findings were compared to theoretical predictions and examined how the band structure changes as the level of excitation increased. The data showed that the energy at which a specific level becomes excited is unaffected by the level of excitation, but instead depends on the core diameter of the nanowire and its specific location within the energy spectrum. The energy at which a specific level becomes excited increased as the level became higher, indicating a specific relationship between these two factors. The energy at which a specific level becomes excited also increased as the level became higher, indicating a specific relationship between these two factors. The energy at which a specific level becomes excited also increased as the core diameter of the nanowire became smaller, indicating a specific relationship between these two factors.
