We have developed a novel method to adjust the mechanical characteristics of bubbles by introducing a thin, rigid layer. The layer, created by depositing nanoparticles on the bubble's surface, enables us to fine-tune the bubble's resonance frequency through layer thickness adjustments via atomic layer deposition. Using this approach, we examined the effects of bubble deformation on their behavior in a water column subjected to acoustic excitation. We observed the coexistence of two distinct bubble populations with varying resonance frequencies, and demonstrated that the bubbles with the higher frequency population are more susceptible to acoustic instability. The ability to adjust bubble properties using this method offers a new pathway for optimizing acoustic cavitation applications.

The growing presence of humans in intelligent systems has led to an increase in research focused on detecting stress, a crucial aspect of human-computer interaction. To address this issue, researchers have developed various machine learning and deep learning models that analyze facial expressions, physiological responses, and other physical indicators of stress. However, the existing literature on stress detection has been hindered by the lack of a unified, emotion-annotated dataset. To address this limitation, we have created a new dataset, the EmotionStress-1k, which consists of 1,000 videos of actors performing different emotions while wearing wearable devices to record physiological data. Our dataset is then used to train and test a state-of-the-art model that combines emotion and stress recognition, which achieved an impressive 85.7% stress detection rate. Our results also highlight the importance of recognizing emotions in identifying stress, which we have demonstrated through experiments on the EmotionStress-1k dataset.

We've developed an enterprise-ready speech annotation tool, designed for large-scale industrial use, and detailed its technical aspects in this paper. To enhance its functionality and facilitate data-driven conversations, we've integrated a robust backend with a cloud database and cloud storage. This setup allows us to provide data-driven insights, analytics, and custom reporting capabilities. Our annotation platform has been successfully deployed at Huawei, where it's facilitated the development of over 1000 custom forms spanning 15 business teams and processed over 1000,000 annotations across a 12-month period.

The initial mass function plays a crucial role in determining the rate at which galaxies are enriched with new elements through supernova explosions, and its variation affects the chemical composition and rate of star formation in galaxies. We have used the FIRE cosmological simulation to examine the variation in the initial mass function across a range of physical conditions, and found that it changes in response to the host galaxy's metal content and star formation rate, with more massive galaxies producing fewer stars. This variation in the initial mass function has a significant impact on the mass of stars produced, with more massive galaxies producing more stars, and we have found that it has a critical effect on the mass of stars produced, with more massive galaxies producing fewer stars due to the initial mass function. We have also found that the initial mass function has a significant effect on the mass of stars produced, with more massive galaxies producing more stars, and this variation is consistent across a range of physical conditions, and is consistent with the variation in the mass of stars produced, with more massive galaxies producing more stars.

Sparse representation using a dictionary is a widely used technique for analyzing signals and data, but its efficiency can be limited due to its high computational requirements when using standard dictionary learning algorithms. To address this issue, we introduce a new approach called the group-based sparse representation method, which enables the learning of sparse representations in a more efficient manner. By grouping the elements of a signal or data point and treating them as a single entity, we can reduce the computational complexity of the sparse representation process. Furthermore, we propose a new greedy pursuit algorithm that accurately reconstructs the data using the group-based sparse representations. The results of our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving high accuracy and efficiency in reconstructing signals and data.

This study introduces a novel object detection network called REthinker, 
which utilizes a unique transformation block to enhance object recognition 
across various scales. The block incorporates a spatial pyramid module to 
improve feature extraction by combining different resolution features. 
Additionally, it incorporates a context module to generate contextual 
features for the classification branch. The network's architecture is 
demonstrated to be highly efficient, with a low computational complexity. 
Extensive experiments were conducted on the MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC datasets, 
yielding highly competitive results. The code for REthinker is publicly 
available.

We establish a worst-case bound on the complexity of sequential decoding for PAC codes, specifically showing that the decoding complexity is capped at a polynomial function of the length $n$ of the code. This worst-case bound is derived from a lower bound on the size of a subset of the error syndromes in a $(2d+1)$-uniform PAC code. Furthermore, we prove that this lower bound applies to a wide range of PAC codes, specifically those with parameters $(n, 2d+1, n-2d)$.

Sequential recommendation models have become a crucial component in various recommendation systems. However, these models often struggle when dealing with users who have limited logged interactions, making it challenging to enhance their predictive power. To address this issue, we introduce MetaTL, a novel approach that utilizes meta-learning techniques to create a unified representation of user-item interactions across multiple datasets. By modeling the transition dynamics between datasets through the transition matrix, MetaTL effectively integrates knowledge from multiple training datasets, resulting in improved sequential recommendation performance. Experimental evaluations on two real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, with results indicating a significant 13.1% improvement in Click-Through Rate (CTR) compared to the baseline model.
The EPOK group has compiled a list of pressing, open research questions in ultra high energy cosmic rays, which are supported by scientific observations and can be addressed through future studies.

A study utilizing the LASSO facility at the University of Bordeaux utilized an array of 36 detectors to analyze the effects of a 1.73 GeV/c projectile on a 3.5 mm thick basalt target.  The enhancement factor for the momentum of protons was calculated in relation to the $p(\alpha)$N elastic scattering at 1.73 GeV, and found to be 0.43.  The data also revealed that the enhancement factor was directly proportional to the square root of the projectile's energy.  The study further examined the correlation between the enhancement factor and the angular distribution of protons, and found that the angular distribution was influenced by the size of the projectile's surface.

We introduce the Mertens Unrolled Network (MU-Net), a deep learning framework designed to create high-resolution, high-quality images of faces behind glass. Building on the concept of Mertens et al.'s, our approach differs by employing a generative model that simulates the optical effects of windshields, rather than a traditional reconstruction network. This innovation enables the simultaneous generation of both the face and the distortions caused by the windshield. Our results demonstrate superior image quality, as evaluated by the Fr\'echet Inception Distance (FID) score and Inception Score (IS), outperforming existing methods by a significant margin. Furthermore, we have made the MU-Net code publicly available.

Packaged distributions of source code software enable developers to share and collaborate on software projects from various platforms by providing a unified view of the codebase, including dependencies and build tools. Building blocks of the code can be easily managed, integrated, and combined to form complex projects. Developers can access, compile, and run the code using a build environment, and the package managers offer additional features such as documentation and testing tools to streamline the development and maintenance process. This paper explores the history and design of the CPAN project, a comprehensive system for Perl software distribution that has been operational since 1991, and draws insights from its 25-year journey. The analysis highlights lessons learned and provides recommendations for other language communities, such as Ruby and Python, to enhance their own software distribution ecosystems.

A new class of models called survival mixture models is proposed in the context of survival analysis. These models incorporate the effects of censoring and missing data through the use of inverse probability weighting and allow for the incorporation of various types of data through different weighting schemes. A two-part model is also presented as a special case of the more general model. A method for estimating the parameters of the data is developed using maximum likelihood estimation. The theoretical properties of the model are investigated under specific assumptions. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated through simulation and applied to real-world data in an integrated analysis.

We introduce a novel function, whose integral can be expressed as a sum of elementary and special functions, and whose asymptotic expansion follows a standard form. Based on this function, we derive new, tighter bounds for the complete elliptic integral of the first kind, specifically for the case where the parameter t is between 0 and 1. These bounds surpass Alzer and Qiu's previous conjectured bounds and recent results from Chihana and Nagai (J. Comput. Appl. Math., 2022), and also improve a bound found in a work by Krucik et al. (J. Math. Anal. Appl., 2019).

Recent advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence have led to significant improvements in the ability of machines to learn from their environments. However, the relationship between the number of examples needed for human and machine learning is still unclear, particularly in the context of complex reinforcement learning tasks. To address this question, we conducted a study in which we compared the performance of both humans and machines in a challenging continuous control task. Our results show that, surprisingly, the number of examples required for both humans and machines to reach a similar level of expertise is relatively small - just 10-20 examples. Moreover, we found that these learning curves follow a similar exponential pattern, suggesting that humans and machines share a common underlying learning mechanism.

In an era of advanced technology, the risk of misinformation has increased, prompting the need for effective solutions to identify manipulated information. Although existing tools are primarily geared towards English-speaking populations, the demand for tools to detect manipulated content in other languages, such as Arabic, is on the rise. To address this need, we have developed the AraNews dataset - a collection of 1,500 news articles, 60% of which are authentic and 40% of which are manipulated, with manipulations ranging from minor to extensive. The dataset, available for download, is a valuable resource for researchers and experts seeking to create detection systems for Arabic news misinformation. To facilitate the creation of such systems, we have also released a pre-trained model, providing a foundation for future work in this area.

A mathematical error in a notable 1963 paper by Ivan Rakhilovich Shafarevich and its subsequent misuse has led to the creation of an artificial theory with numerous problems. This incorrect theory claims the existence of specific fields within a certain category based on flawed reasoning. This brief article aims to correct the errors, demonstrating that the mentioned fields do not exist, thereby resolving the related issues.

The correlation functions between qubits typically decrease with distance, but in specific cases, they remain unaffected by spatial separation. This unusual behavior is linked to the transfer of information through a continuous energy field, exemplified by the ground state of a system consisting of two levels of energy that are equally spaced. This model can be expanded to include multiple energy levels, and its properties can be understood through the lens of quasiparticles called "information quasiparticles." These particles have distinct characteristics, such as a specific effective mass, in the extended model, and their interaction with the system's energy levels leads to the transfer of information over varying distances. The model can be applied to various physical systems, including quantum dots, atomic ensembles, and superconducting devices, to describe both the transfer of information and the decoherence process.

Focused crawling involves selectively choosing web pages relevant to a specific topic, often in response to a query.  Existing methods for this process rely on either pre-existing or user-generated criteria, but the decision on which page to crawl next is made without consideration of the criteria.  We propose the Tree-Frontier algorithm, which optimizes the action of selecting a page to crawl by taking into account both the criteria for importance and the criteria for relevance.  This approach is based on a decision tree model, where the goal is to achieve the highest possible outcome (i.e., a leaf node representing a page of interest).  In our implementation, the decision tree is represented as a directed graph, and the algorithm iteratively explores this graph, giving greater weight to nodes that are more likely to result in a successful crawl.  We have tested the Tree-Frontier algorithm using data from Bing and evaluated its performance in comparison to existing methods.  Our results show that the Tree-Frontier algorithm outperforms the other methods, achieving a higher precision rate and a higher recall rate while minimizing the number of crawled pages.

Traditional process mining techniques rely on event logs capturing specific process executions. However, these techniques struggle with understanding process dynamics when only aggregate, group-level information is available. To address this limitation, a new approach is proposed to analyze the dynamics of group-level processes using object-centric event data. This approach is centered around a new measure called the Object-centric Process View, which visualizes process dynamics by mapping object relationships to process features. By applying this measure, it is possible to uncover process features, identify causal object relationships, and forecast the future state of a process. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through experiments on real event data and a synthetic dataset.

A novel, computationally efficient method for seismic wavefield recovery has been developed. This method, built upon the simultaneous orthogonal upsampling technique, allows for the accurate recovery of missing wavefield data within a specified spatial domain. By iteratively applying a 2D Fourier Split Radon Transform and performing upsampling in the transformed domain, the proposed method effectively restores the lost wavefield data. Successful field test results demonstrate that this method can fully restore 2D/3D wavefields with high precision, making it a valuable tool for seismic interpretation and modeling processes.

A silicon metalens that can simultaneously control phase, amplitude, and phase gradient was designed and fabricated. The metalens, made using a single silicon layer, was fabricated using a process that combines the definition of the phase gradient with that of the phase and amplitude. At 20 GHz, it demonstrated a 140-degree field of view and 2.2 GHz bandwidth, with an 8.5dB linear scan sensitivity. The metalen's unique phase gradient enabled a high-frequency beam stability of 3.5 degrees, even in the presence of phase errors.

The dynamics of a group of electrons within a plasma are studied, and it's found that their spatial and temporal development aligns with Poisson-Boltzmann equilibrium under certain conditions. The electrons' movement towards a plasma state is influenced by a non-linear equation that reflects the self-gravity of ions and electrostatic effects. The study reveals that the electrons' distribution function conforms to a Bose-Einstein form with a non-traditional temperature measurement based on the distance from the plasma. The non-linear equation describing their movement is a combination of the Poisson equation and the quantum Boltzmann equation. The study also identifies a quantum component to the electrons' distribution function, and it's found that the system can transition to a steady state with a non-equilibrium plasma shape. The system's temperature and potential function are both dependent on the electrons' distribution function, and these functions are correlated with the system's temperature and potential function.

The quasinormal frequencies of scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational waves around a higher-dimensional Kerr black hole exhibit a direct relationship with its unstable circular orbits. Specifically, the imaginary components of these frequencies align with the principal Lyapunov exponent at each unstable orbit. Furthermore, the separation between stable and unstable orbits in the complex frequency plane can be accurately described by a Chebyshev polynomial of order one less than that of the corresponding circular orbit.

Pulsar Timing Arrays, which monitor the diffuse background noise generated by numerous pulsars, have the potential to detect faint, diffuse sources that may not be apparent at individual pulsar observations. The current sensitivity of these arrays is limited by their ability to process individual pulsar data, but future improvements could enable them to analyze data from all pulsars simultaneously, allowing for more detailed searches for sources like gravitational waves. The potential for discovering sources through this method is investigated by analyzing the characteristics of the background noise and comparing the results to predictions made by radio interferometry.

Research on linear code generalized minimum distance (GM-MDS) construction has been ongoing for years. Initially, the GM-MDS conjecture was proposed by Yan and Deng in 2012, but it was later found that the direct generalization of this conjecture for 2-MDS codes and algebraic geometry codes is not applicable to fields of any size. In response to this issue, further studies were conducted to explore the GM-MDS code construction within specific smaller field settings. In this study, we present a new GM-MDS construction for linear codes over finite fields of odd characteristics, and we provide examples of GM-MDS codes.

The kernel of a matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator can be expressed as the sum of four separate components, with each term corresponding to a smaller dimensional matrix. The first two components correspond to backward and forward shifts within a larger space, while the remaining terms represent such shifts within smaller spaces. This decomposition serves as a matrix analogue to Carathéodory's theorem and has the added benefit of being applicable to matrix-valued shift operators of any size.

This research examines a scenario in which an informed sender attempts to convince an uninformed receiver by sending a message. Although the sender's messages have a known distribution, their effect on the receiver is uncertain. A sequence of non-random messages can be used to achieve this goal, with the sender's influence on the receiver determined by a state that is influenced by these messages. The sender's ultimate goal is to maximize the receiver's value in the worst case, with the sender's communication channel subject to bandwidth limitations. The study reveals that optimal communication often involves a strategic approach, and a dynamic programming method is used to calculate the sender's optimal behavior. The study also considers the scenario where the sender's message is restricted in size and presents an algorithm to find the sender's optimal behavior in this case.

The goal of Unsupervised Anomaly Detection under Domain Shift Conditions (UAD-S) is to identify anomalies in new environments without labeled data.  Current methods are limited by their inability to accurately capture the impact of contextual changes on anomaly detection, which results in poor generalizability to diverse environments.  To address this issue, we introduce a framework called Contextual Anomaly Detection (CAD) that considers the effects of contextual changes on anomalies.  CAD employs a novel domain shift metric called Contextual Shift Metric (CSM) and a contextual anomaly detection method called Contextual Anomaly Detection Network (CADNet).  CSM measures the changes in contextual patterns between training and testing environments, while CADNet uses a contrastive learning approach to learn the normal and anomalous patterns in the training environment.  Our experiments on UAD-S datasets show that CAD outperforms existing methods and provides insights into the impact of contextual changes on anomaly detection.

We examine the ground state of a Fermi gas confined in a one-dimensional ring with attractive interactions and spin greater than or equal to half. We find that the previously predicted phase transition from a superfluid to a topological superfluid for spin 1/2 is indeed valid. However, for larger spin values, the transition becomes a first-order change rather than the originally predicted second-order one. We also explore the effects of this transition on systems with a limited number of particles.

The relationship between the pulsar power and the pair production boundary is examined. The shift in this boundary is investigated over time for pulsars that have a gradual decrease in their rotational energy output due to operational magnetic pole models. The effect of varying magnetic pole models on the relationship between the pulsar power and the pair production boundary is studied. The long-term shift in the gamma-ray 'death line' is found to be relatively small, approximately 0.1-0ms in magnitude, and is mainly caused by the change in the pulsar's surface dipole magnetic field. The effect of this shift on the population of observed pulsars is found to be minimal. The primary source of this shift in the gamma-ray 'death line' is actually the change in the pulsar's rotational energy loss rate, which is caused by the decrease in the pulsar's surface dipole magnetic field. The effect of this shift on the population of observed pulsars is found to be significant, and is mainly caused by the change in the pulsar's surface dipole magnetic field. The long-term shift in the gamma-ray 'death line' is found to be in agreement with the observed gamma-ray pulsar population. The effect of this shift on the population of observed pulsars is found to be significant, and is mainly caused by the change in the pulsar's surface dipole magnetic field.

The quantum Hall effect in twisted bilayers of graphene exhibits a unique feature where the lowest energy state can change based on the twist angle. This change can occur at specific angles, specifically $\theta = 10.85^\circ$, where the phase transitions occur. Researchers have been studying the rotational motion of the bilayers, known as magnetorotons, to gain insight into the properties of twisted bilayers. A study has been conducted on the magnetorotons within the two distinct phases of the $\theta = 10.85^\circ$ state, specifically the $\mu = 2/7$ state and the $\mu = 2/9$ state. The study found that magnetorotons in the $\mu = 2/7$ state display a left-right asymmetry, whereas those in the $\mu = 2/9$ state display a symmetry consistent with a classical model. The study suggests that the observed chirality in the $\mu = 2/7$ state is a direct result of the phase transition, whereas the observed left-right symmetry in the $\mu = 2/9$ state is a direct result of the phase transition failure. The study found that the observed chirality in the $\mu = 2/7$ state is a direct result of the phase transition, whereas the observed left-right symmetry in the $\mu = 2/9$ state is a direct result of the phase transition failure.

The Italian EEO telescope, a 60cm aperture wide-field telescope, is a part of the EEE observational network. Comprised of various telescopes, including 40cm 40cm, 60cm and 1m aperture systems, this network spans across multiple locations in Italy such as Bologna, Florence, Padova, Toulouse, and Noto. The Italian EEE observatory, situated at Bologna, is equipped with a 60cm aperture telescope and a 2.0m telescope. The latter is a unique, 2.0m aperture telescope featuring a 7.5m long focal length and a 2048x2048 CCD detector. The Italian EEE observatory, responsible for conducting approximately 20% of scientific surveys, plays a significant role in the ATLAS collaboration within the Dark Energy Survey. The Italian EEE observatory, in collaboration with other European facilities, has successfully completed the ATLAS Dark Energy Survey, which aims to understand the expansion history of the universe. The Italian EEE observatory, in partnership with other European facilities, has also contributed to the development of the Kilo-Degree Survey, which focuses on understanding the structure of the universe at smaller scales. This paper explores the global solution to the $\gamma$-regularized Boltzmann equation, known as the cutoff Boltzmann equation with $\gamma \in (0,1]$. The approach involves a functional method that yields a quantitative upper bound for the solution $f^\gamma(t,x)$ and proves that this solution converges to the solution of the traditional Boltzmann equation as $\gamma$ approaches $0$. Moreover, the solution's behavior shifts from smooth to singular as $\gamma$ varies from $0$ to $1$.

This study examines the dual role of adversarial training in enhancing robustness and reducing overfitting. Our findings indicate that models trained on noisy data for robustness exhibit superior performance when tested on clean data, while those trained with regularization for reduced overfitting fare worse. This disparity suggests that to minimize overfitting, the training set should focus on clean samples, while noisy data is more effective for evaluating generalization accuracy. Consequently, models should be trained using a combination of noisy and clean data to leverage their distinct strengths.

We provide a straightforward criterion for identifying linear isometries that link distinct cyclic orbit codes. In addition, we examine the scenario where a linear isometry exists between two distinct cyclic orbit codes, $C\subseteq C_{1}$ and $C\subseteq C_{2}$, having the same base field and of equal lengths, assuming a common generator exists for these codes.

A binary star system consisting of WOCS 11028A and B was discovered in the M67 cluster, with the primary component being a G3 Ab/Shell star and the secondary a $\delta$ Sct star. The binary's discovery was facilitated by high-resolution imaging and spectroscopy, with the primary component identified through spectroscopy and photometry, and further supported by astrometry and spectro-astrometry. The binary's separation of 2.59 arcseconds and velocity of 33.0 km/s relative to the cluster center make it a challenging system to resolve. The primary component was found to be 0.8 magnitudes below the turnoff point of the cluster, with a mass estimated at 1.22 solar masses, while its age and metallicity were found to be consistent with the cluster's properties. The secondary component was found to be a $\delta$ Sct star with a mass estimated at 1.64 solar masses, with a period of 0.4446 days, an amplitude of 0.15 mag, and a range of frequencies corresponding to the $\delta$ Sct instability strip. The binary's properties were further analyzed through light curves and spectral analysis, with the primary component exhibiting shell activity and the secondary component displaying a $\delta$ Sct-like light curve.

We examine the eigenfunctions of the fractional Laplacian within the context of a finite volume. Specifically, we analyze the eigenfunctions of the operator $(-\Delta)^{1/2}-c/(8\pi)^{1/4}\delta(r)\}$, where $c$ is a complex parameter. Our research demonstrates that for $c$'s argument falling within the range $(-2,2)$, a set of eigenfunctions is both linearly independent and covers the entire space, providing an innovative application of the Borel Perel'man Tail Estimate. Our findings also yield an explicit upper limit on the spectral measure of an eigenfunction.

A recent study on GSPH methods revealed that varying the type of volume elements leads to inconsistencies in mass conservation. This paper aims to address this limitation by developing a comprehensive framework that reconciles different volume elements within a single GSPH formalism. By incorporating a flexible weighting scheme for volume elements, we can derive an adaptable GSPH formalism that supports various volume elements such as Warren's hexahedral, moving least squares, and simplex types. This unified approach is then applied to particle-based hydrodynamics, demonstrating the influence of volume elements on gradient estimation. Our findings indicate that volume element choice has a profound impact on gradient estimation accuracy, which is further examined through numerical experiments.

This paper introduces a novel deep learning approach for converting RGB images into hyperspectral images. The proposed method utilizes a function-mixture network that is aware of pixel-level characteristics. A novel loss function, grounded in spectral similarity, is developed to optimize the network's performance. Additionally, a new strategy for initializing network weights is designed to enhance the model's generalization capabilities. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on real-world hyperspectral image datasets.

This study introduces a novel, deep learning-based framework for pinpointing street objects. Leveraging the strengths of BERT to capture contextual information, our method combines it with a Convolutional Neural Network to tap into the object's visual characteristics. By integrating these two components, we enhance the accuracy of geolocation predictions. Notably, our model's performance surpasses existing approaches without relying on a pre-trained global model. To demonstrate its versatility, we also explore how our model can learn from maps, both manually annotated and generated through random forest regression, in both supervised and semi-supervised learning settings.

This paper introduces a novel approach to dam reservoir classification using remote sensing data, incorporating metric learning to enhance the classification process. The proposed method involves a two-stage process where the first stage learns a suitable metric from a set of embeddings, and the second stage utilizes this metric to perform classification. The resulting system is tested on a large dataset from South Africa and achieves a high success rate, with results indicating a significant improvement over previous approaches. The proposed system is also shown to perform well when faced with data imbalances, achieving a high AUC score of 0.93.

We've developed a new class of spaces called QFS-spaces which contain a continuous, one-to-one mapping to Euclidean space yet have properties allowing for smooth local transformations. This space is a more comprehensive version of the previously studied FS-space. Our research shows that continuous projections exist within QFS-spaces and we've also established a connection between QFS-spaces and retracts of Euclidean space. Furthermore, our findings indicate that QFS-spaces possess a unique combination of features - they are locally compact, star-shaped, and have properties allowing for a continuous transformation into Euclidean space.

We introduce a novel multimodal approach to predicting points of interest, utilizing both text and visual data. Our model is trained on a large dataset of Wikipedia articles related to multiple languages, and we evaluate its performance on several benchmark datasets. Notably, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on the Google Multi-Language Wikipedia dataset, outperforming previous methods with a significant increase in accuracy. Our findings also suggest that combining text and visual data is essential for achieving superior performance.

This study examines the connection between earnings call conversations and subsequent stock price movements. It's known that investors often base their decisions on company management's interpretations of financial health and future prospects, rather than solely focusing on hard financial metrics. To explore this dynamic better, the researchers analyzed a dataset of earnings call transcripts and a corresponding set of stock price movements. They used a technique called topic modeling to identify key themes within these conversations and discovered that the semantic topics in these discussions can provide valuable insights into stock performance. In fact, the semantic topics were found to offer better predictive power than established financial metrics, such as the Z-score. To further investigate the relationship between these topics and stock movements, the researchers developed a new model that incorporates both topic weights and financial metrics to make more accurate predictions. The results showed that incorporating semantic topics can significantly improve the accuracy of predictions, particularly in specific market conditions.

This paper examines the effectiveness of a wireless sensor network in detecting the location of a target when its communication range is restricted. By employing a Bayesian approach, we derive the optimal sensor network configuration in terms of number and placement to maximize the reliability of the detection. Utilizing the method of Green's function in three-dimensional space to model the wave propagation, we establish an equation to calculate the probability of successful detection. Through the use of asymptotic analysis, we develop a simplified analytical formula for the most efficient sensor placement, taking into account the trade-off between the sensors' directional characteristics and the network's reduced communication range. Our theoretical findings are supported by numerical simulations.

We've developed a new quantum algorithm for determining the closest vector to a given set of points under matrix multiplication. The algorithm uses a quantum walk approach and can handle sparse matrices. It's particularly efficient when the number of points to check is much smaller than the matrix's size. The algorithm's performance is measured by how long it takes to make each query, and its speed depends on how sparse the matrix is. For very dense matrices, the algorithm uses a query time of O(s/N) that improves to O(1/N) when the matrix is very sparse. The algorithm's performance matches what's theoretically possible and improves upon previous methods.

The Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis in a nonlinear dielectric medium within a confined space is analyzed. Assuming a constant source of signal and a fixed, bounded area, we prove the existence of a non-singular solution using a perturbation approach, building on the compactness of the base acting as a reference solution. Furthermore, we establish the global existence of a non-singular compacton solution and examine the influence of the medium's nonlinearity on compacton profiles, showing that stronger nonlinearity results in steeper compactons and increased front speeds.

The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) is a versatile framework for analyzing how the standard model might be expanded to include new interactions among known particles. This text outlines a practical approach to employing SMEFT in the pursuit of new physics through the examination of two key processes: Higgs boson production and single top quark production. By presenting case studies that demonstrate how SMEFT's constraints on the theory's parameters can be derived from experimental data, the text aims to illustrate SMEFT's effectiveness in identifying the standard model's weaknesses and the potential implications for the theory's extensions. This text is intended as a starting point for further exploration and discussion of the topics addressed.

A miniature all-optical laser-based rotation sensor is developed, which can simultaneously measure a specific rotation and its sensitivity to temperature fluctuations. By employing a dual-interferometer design, the sensor's performance is enhanced. In the conventional setup, the rotation and phase reflection errors are intertwined, whereas the modified sensor separates these errors through an innovative arrangement. In the standard protocol, the sensor's sensitivity to temperature fluctuations is heightened, whereas the modified one remains robust. In the modified sensor, the phase modulation technique is utilized to enhance the rotation signal. A novel method is proposed to eliminate the phase reflection error without introducing additional optical components. In the modified sensor, the resolution is significantly improved, reaching as high as 0.1 deg/hr, by leveraging the benefits of dual-interferometers and phase modulation.

The development of comprehensive whole-cell models holds significant promise in both biological and medical research, with machine learning and artificial intelligence playing a crucial role in this endeavor. These models will enable the integration of multiple data types and analysis techniques, allowing researchers to simulate cellular behavior and make predictions about cellular responses to different stimuli. This can be achieved by analyzing high-dimensional data from various omics studies, which can be complemented by machine learning methods that can analyze data across multiple scales simultaneously. Furthermore, the use of digital twins will facilitate the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence to biological systems, while addressing the associated ethical complexities.

This paper introduces a novel object image search method that leverages the benefits of multi-view images over single-view images. By treating object images as complex, context-rich documents, we've developed an innovative retrieval technique that capitalizes on the rich contextual information within multi-view images. Our approach involves creating a unique, context-aware representation for each object image by combining the global features of individual views and contextual features that capture the relationships between views. This representation is then used to index object images for efficient querying. Experimental results on various multi-view image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, which significantly outperforms traditional baselines.

This paper introduces a cutting-edge hybrid technique that integrates multi-centroid and multi-pass learning methods for distinguishing and categorizing epileptic seizures from normal electroencephalogram readings. The proposed strategy is applied to 23 patients' data, which includes 24-hour recordings of two channels' activity. The outcomes of this approach are compared to those of other established algorithms. The results show that the integrated learning strategy outperforms other methods, with a 95.5% success rate in detecting seizures and a 96.1% success rate in predicting seizure duration. This indicates that the integrated learning strategy can provide more accurate analysis of EEG readings to identify seizure types and durations.

We examine the potential of using gravitational wave sources with electromagnetic counterparts to measure the Hubble constant, H0, through the dark siren method. By assuming a gravitational wave signal model with a power-law top-halfline morphology, we analyze the accuracy of measuring distances to these sources. We then determine the expected precision of measuring H0 by combining the distances with electromagnetic data from sources such as binary black holes, neutron stars, and giant stars. Our findings indicate that future gravitational wave observations with enhanced detector sensitivity could yield an error margin of approximately 2% on the H0 measurement.

The QALD-9 dataset, initially designed for KGQA systems to process natural language queries and retrieve graph answers, is expanded to include more diverse questions and languages. This updated dataset, known as QALD-9-plus, incorporates 1,100 new questions and 2,000 answers from the QuAD dataset in English, as well as 1,100 questions and 2,100 answers in Hindi. The enhanced dataset is utilized to evaluate the performance of KGQA systems on a range of multilingual question answering tasks. The results indicate that the addition of the new questions and languages from QALD-9-plus poses significant challenges to KGQA systems.

This study introduces an innovative perspective on learning theory, rooted in the concept of hindsight summarization. By utilizing this approach, we demonstrate its potential to minimize prediction errors over time, particularly when learning from complex datasets. The proposed method is applied to the regression task, where individual data points are represented as vectors, and their corresponding outcomes are related through a linear function. By condensing past data observations into a concise summary, we can improve the efficiency of our learning algorithm and potentially reduce the number of training samples required.

Medical image analysis relies heavily on deep learning methods, but these approaches can inadvertently inherit and propagate implicit biases present in their training datasets, ultimately hindering their performance in real-world applications. To shed light on this issue, we conducted a comprehensive study focusing on the impact of dataset-specific biases on the generalizability of image analysis models. Our research involved a detailed examination of the effects of dataset-specific biases on the generalizability of image analysis models, specifically in the context of chest X-ray images. We used a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods to investigate how these biases affect the models' performance, and our findings indicate that demographic-specific biases are indeed transferred to the models. Moreover, we discovered that these biases are not unique to one specific aspect of the images, but can be found in various components, such as image texture and shape. Furthermore, we found that these biases are not solely caused by differences in patient demographics, but can be a result of various factors, including differences in equipment and scanning protocols. To mitigate these biases, we also explored the effectiveness of data augmentation techniques, and our results suggest that these methods can be a useful approach to reducing bias in medical image analysis models.

This research introduces a new loss function called Smooth Proxy-Anchor Loss, designed to improve the performance of Metric Learning methods. It achieves this by creating a loss function that smooths out the effects of outliers in the data, by introducing a new metric that measures the distance between the data points and the anchor points. The anchor points are chosen by first clustering the data points and then using each cluster as an anchor point. The approach was tested on various datasets for both classification and clustering tasks, resulting in significant improvements over existing methods when compared to the baseline.

We've developed a new method for calculating weighted statistics that uses a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm, focusing on galaxy clustering data. This method differs from previous density-based weighting methods in its gradient-based approach, which allows for more precise parameter estimation by reducing the bias in the data. However, this also makes the method more prone to over-fitting. To mitigate this issue, we're introducing a new regularization technique that utilizes a penalty term to enforce a minimum distance between data points in the parameter space. This method is being tested on galaxy mock catalogs generated by the Baryons in Dark Energy Survey (BOSS) and the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation. Our results show that the new method outperforms the density-based method in terms of parameter estimation accuracy, with significant improvements in the constraints on cosmological parameters such as the matter density parameter, the amplitude of matter fluctuations, and the Hubble constant.

We have developed a novel approach to study superfluids in the presence of external magnetic fields. By incorporating the effects of the external magnetic field into the action integral's exchange energy, we can derive the Landau-Ginzburg equation. This leads to the well-known Josephson current equation. Our method is applied to investigate the influence of the external magnetic field on the critical current in a Josephson junction. Furthermore, we discuss the implications of time-dependent magnetic fields on the Josephson current.

Large Area Picosecond Photomultiplier Detectors consist of a collection of MAPPDs, each equipped with a photodetector and an associated electronics system, which capture gamma-ray signals and output data for analysis. These detectors are highly sensitive due to their large active areas and picoseond temporal resolution. Their performance can be optimized by adjusting parameters such as spatial resolution, energy sensitivity, and timing precision. These parameters are influenced by the geometry of the detectors and the characteristics of the detected gamma rays. To optimize the performance of LAPPD, a detailed understanding of the detector's response to high-energy gamma rays is essential. In this study, a LAPPD system was exposed to a high-energy gamma-ray source and the output was analyzed. The analysis involved measuring the timing resolution of the detectors and the energy deposition in the detector, and comparing the results to a simulation. The study also explored the relationship between the timing resolution and energy deposition, and the potential for using this relationship to improve the detector's timing precision.

This paper provides an alternative method for calculating sectional genera in specific forms of local Gorenstein rings that are complete Gorenstein Gorenstein domains. Furthermore, it demonstrates the application of sectional genera in characterizing these domains as complete Gorenstein Gorenstein domains. The findings are then applied to characterize and define complete Gorenstein domains with a particular form in a different manner.

The effect of hydrostatic pressure on the structure of Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ was studied using X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy. The application of increasing pressure led to a phase transition from a room temperature structure to a more ordered arrangement at 2.33 GPa. The transition was confirmed by changes in the Raman spectrum and X-ray diffraction patterns. The transition pressure was found to be consistent with previous findings. The application of pressure resulted in significant lattice parameter changes, particularly in the $a$ and $b$ parameters, while the $c$ parameter showed minimal variation. The Raman shifts in the low-frequency mode also indicated a phase transition. The results suggest that Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ has a complex structure and that the application of pressure can significantly alter its properties.

A recently developed, open-source tool called PyTARDIS offers a platform for comparing broker algorithms in relation to exchange fees by using historical trade data. However, the tool's reporting capabilities focus solely on broker performance metrics relative to the exchange fees. To address this limitation, we propose employing a Bayesian framework to assess the statistical significance of broker performance metrics in relation to the exchange fees. Our approach enhances the tool's utility in evaluating broker algorithms, particularly in facilitating collaborative research by allowing scientists to pool and compare results across diverse datasets using the same statistical framework. To demonstrate the utility of our method, we demonstrate its application in analyzing the performance of well-established brokers when trained on either the Nasdaq or NYSE data sets.

A newly developed, broadly tunable optical filter allows for the simultaneous tuning of a specific wavelength across a range of 30 nm and a surrounding wavelength across a range of 10 nm, achieving tunability of the filter's free-spectral range. The filter's design utilizes a silicon waveguide with a sub-wavelength slot and builds upon existing work in [1] and [2]. By adjusting the refractive index of the slot through the use of a thermoelectric heater, the filter exhibits minimal changes in performance, including insertion loss and flatness, across the tuning range. Experimental results show that the filter's insertion loss remains consistently low at less than 5 dB across the tuning range, and the filter's flatness remains at less than 5 percent. Furthermore, the filter's design allows for the simultaneous tuning of the filter across the tuning range in less than 30 milliseconds. The filter's design also enables the tuning of the filter's bandwidth by adjusting the length of the slot, which can be achieved through the use of a micro-electromechanical system.

Disease modeling based on online information can provide insights into the effectiveness of vaccination efforts, enable early detection of new outbreaks, and predict the impact of different interventions. A key challenge in this process involves analyzing a vast array of online data to identify relevant patterns and trends. To address this challenge, we have developed a new method that utilizes a combination of supervised learning and self-supervised learning techniques to identify sensitive disease-related patterns in time-series data. Our approach can effectively capture a wide range of temporal patterns, including seasonal fluctuations and non-linear trends, and has been demonstrated to be effective in extracting sensitive information from both simulated and real-world datasets.

We introduce a novel image compression framework, called PILC, designed to outperform the widely used PNG standard. Our framework's key innovation lies in the application of Learned Compression Functions, utilizing deep neural networks to process data, without relying on explicit statistical models. This approach enables PILC to compress images more effectively, using fewer parameters than existing state-of-the-art solutions. Our experiments demonstrate PILC's superiority over PNG, as well as its competitive performance compared to top-tier methods. Notably, PILC achieves significant size reductions of up to 26% across multiple image datasets and outperforms PNG by an average of 12%.

An analysis of a $B^{+} \to D^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decay candidate, verified by verifying the $B^{+} \to D^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decay, and requiring the additional presence of two pions, was conducted using 3 fb$^{-1}$ of LHCb data obtained at 7 and 8 TeV centre-of-mass energies. The resulting $B^{+}$ signal is identified as a $D^{+}$ signal with a mass of 1965.16 MeV/$c^{2}$ and a $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ mass of 1.04 GeV/$c^{2}$, consistent with a $B^{+} \to D^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decay. The $B^{+} \to D^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ branching fraction is estimated to be around $(2.8 \pm 0.5 \pm 0.3 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-7}$, with a 95% confidence level upper limit of $3.6 \times 10^{-7}$ for the $B^{+} \to D^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decay, and no significant evidence for a $B^{+} \to D

The core idea of optimal transport is measuring distance between distributions by minimizing cost, but it's sensitive to irregularities and anomalies. This paper presents a robust alternative, building upon a previous approach, by assigning lower costs to normal data points and higher costs to irregular ones. The assignment is made by evaluating the local density of data points relative to their neighborhood. The resulting robust distance is demonstrated to be mathematically equivalent to a related problem involving a regularization term. The proposed approach is shown to be more effective in real-world applications compared to existing methods through experimental analysis.

To achieve human-like intelligence in teaming with humans, AI must be designed to learn and adapt through collaborative experiences. We propose exploring a unique learning path – complementing human strategies – to significantly boost AI's performance in teaming. By leveraging minimal human input, our system identifies and imitates exceptional approaches in complex decision-making scenarios. We have developed a general framework for this approach, tested it in the context of the first annual Microsoft Malware Prediction Challenge, where it successfully outperformed top competitors in both accuracy and efficiency.

The Generation Split spectrum, a component of the Gensplit model, is a key area of focus in Beyond Standard Model (BSM) research due to its potential for new physics signals. The Gensplit model offers a comprehensive framework that naturally incorporates the Standard Model, with the Generation Split spectrum serving as a key indicator of proton decay and neutrino mass generation. The Gensplit model is a well-defined, UV-complete theory that predicts the masses of all Standard Model fermions, including a specific value for the top quark mass. The Gensplit model's predictions for the Generation Split spectrum, particularly in its perturbative regime, are a crucial aspect of this framework. The implications of this spectrum, including its potential for new physics signals and the constraints it places on parameter space, are an active area of research. The Gensplit model's predictions for the Generation Split spectrum, including its potential for new physics signals and the constraints it places on parameter space, are an interesting area of study.

A 2012 New York Times article on the rise of international migration may have misused a pie chart, prompting widespread criticism. Yet, in their quest to create effective visualizations, many designers often overlook pie charts in favor of more intricate alternatives. Contrary to conventional wisdom, our research suggests that pie charts can be just as effective as other visualizations in most cases. In a series of studies involving various tasks, we compared pie charts to more complex visualizations, such as bar charts and treemaps, in different domains, including data aggregation and categorical composition. Our findings indicate that simpler visualizations tend to perform better on aggregate tasks, whereas more complex visualizations excel at categorical analysis. Notably, domain expertise plays a crucial role in this performance disparity. For instance, demographers specializing in international migration performed significantly better with pie charts, whereas experts from other fields, including those in data science, fared worse with more complex visualizations.

We examine the connection between induction and fixpoint logic in the presence of a cycle of clause sets that include open premises, as well as the associated problems that arise. This issue is relevant in the field of formalizations of mathematical theories, particularly when dealing with incomplete axiomatizations of mathematical structures. Our study is divided into two sections. Firstly, we investigate the relationship between induction and cycles of clause sets, taking into account open premises, and propose a method to address this challenge. Secondly, we explore the possibility of encoding cycles using least fixed-point logic, and propose a modified approach that allows for the use of a more flexible operator, referred to as the $PL$-operator.

The Shortest Path Kernel is a well-known and efficient graph similarity measure that has been applied to graph matching, retrieval, and comparison tasks. However, its computational complexity grows rapidly due to the use of Dijkstra's algorithm, making it unsuitable for large-scale graph processing. In this research, a modified version of the Shortest Path Kernel is proposed to accelerate its computation and improve its performance, and we validate its effectiveness through experiments on various benchmark datasets.

To improve the accuracy of simulations modeling transient physical phenomena, we've developed a novel machine learning approach. This method, based on a combination of self-supervised and supervised learning techniques, allows us to represent complex dynamics using reduced-dimensional representations and is particularly effective when paired with an advanced neural network model. This method has been successfully applied to a dynamic spring model, where it accurately replicated the behavior of the original system, even in cases where it was given no initial data or only partial information. Furthermore, we've demonstrated the ability to iteratively refine our model by using it to generate new data, which can then be used to improve the accuracy of our simulations.

In modern times, electricity distribution is a critical issue. This paper addresses the challenge of allocating costs among neighbors who share a downed power line, which we model as a combinatorial fair division problem. We develop an algorithm that enables participants to achieve a 3/m-approximation solution in polynomials of m objects with limited communication and for m+1 participants. We further investigate this problem within the context of the Chef Goes to a Party combinatorial cake-cutting problem and establish a 3/2-approximation solution for the electricity distribution problem using the proportional sharing curve.

Accurately identifying and organizing events in text is crucial for analyzing and understanding complex events and relationships between them. To achieve this, we propose a two-stage approach that uses event coreference resolution to enhance event information collection. The approach involves a model that first recognizes event mentions in sentences, then clusters these mentions into event instances. The model utilizes a BERT-based encoder to extract event and coreference characteristics, which are then combined using a graph neural network to generate event instances. To prevent the model from overfitting, we incorporate a BERT-based decoder and a graph attention-based decoder. To address the imbalance issue in event mentions, we propose a multi-task learning framework that includes event coreference resolution and mention normalization tasks. Experimental results on two Chinese event datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving event normalization accuracy and resolving coreference.

This paper presents novel facet-defining inequalities for the complementarity knapsack problem. These inequalities were discovered through the generation of valid inequalities in mixed-integer programming formulations for the complementarity knapsack problem. We validated the efficacy of our approach by identifying new valid inequalities that define facets in specific problem instances, and also explored the broader implications of our research.

Our research focuses on the properties of generalized $(m,n)$-Jordan centralizers in the context of non-associative rings. We establish that these generalized operators are specifically $(m,n)$-Jordan centralizers when subject to torsion restrictions. We also examine their relationship with generalized Jordan derivations as well as the spectral properties of generalized Jordan derivations under these same restrictions.

We investigate the role of Winger constraints in the formation of the Weinberg soft factor, an essential element in the resummation of next-to-next-to-next-to leading logarithmic soft anomalous dimensions at very low momentum transfer. Our analysis demonstrates that these constraints are crucial in creating a consistent cohomological structure, ultimately ensuring the symmetry of the integrand at all orders in perturbation theory.

We examine the constraint for two orthogonal projections to be separable in a real Hilbert space and show that this separability condition implies a specific transversality property in the projections. Furthermore, we consider projections onto closed subspaces and establish a separability criterion in terms of the intersection of these subspaces. Our investigation also involves a more general class of nonlinear projection-type operators and explores the transversality properties associated with their separability. Ultimately, we apply our findings to certain nonlinear mappings, including those involving additive and multiplicative operators, as well as symmetric and positive definite projections.

In imitation learning, a model is trained to replicate expert behavior by leveraging demonstrations.  However, a critical concern arises when the environment undergoes a change due to uncertainty about the nature of the shift.  To address this challenge, we examine the relationship between the efficiency of demonstrations and the capacity to adapt to shifting environmental conditions.  Specifically, we establish a theoretical connection between demonstration efficiency and the resilience of imitation learning algorithms in the face of uncertainty.  Furthermore, we propose a novel metric called the $\epsilon$-demonstration efficiency, which is grounded in the concept of $\epsilon$-optimal paths in Markov decision processes.  This metric is shown to be sufficient to ensure the adaptability of imitation learning algorithms in the presence of uncertainty.  Our findings are substantiated through experiments on discrete and continuous domains.

The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (I-AHE) is typically associated with materials that break time-reversal symmetry through an external magnetic field. However, we have conducted a comprehensive examination of the I-AHE in magnetically stable materials that do not require an external magnetic field to exhibit this phenomenon. By applying a symmetry analysis, we have identified the conditions necessary for I-AHE to occur in certain types of hexagonal and rectangular lattices. Our analysis has also taken into account the impact of different spin-orbit coupling mechanisms and has considered the effects of various lattice configurations. By using a tight-binding model, we have demonstrated that these materials can exhibit significant topological anomalies, including values of the AHE conductivity, $\sigma_{xy}$, as large as $10^4\sigma_0$.

To optimize performance in complex systems, understanding the actual execution context is crucial. However, current performance optimization methods are often based on outdated assumptions about the execution context, leading to suboptimal results. To bridge this gap, we developed a new approach that utilizes call graph data to identify key execution contexts and compare them to the data in performance profiles, allowing us to pinpoint the most critical bottlenecks. By doing so, we can provide a more accurate and context-specific analysis of performance issues, enabling more effective optimizations. Our approach has been implemented as a tool called Context-O, which is available for public use.

The One Billion Word Benchmark (OBDM) has been widely regarded as the industry standard for evaluating language models' capacity. However, we argue that the OBDM only assesses a limited aspect of a language model's capabilities, and we explore its shortcomings in this regard. By using the OBDM, a model can primarily learn to predict the next word in a sequence, rather than truly capturing the complexities of language. To demonstrate this, we compare the OBDM to a more comprehensive benchmark that assesses a model's ability to capture the nuances of language through its representation of word meanings. Our findings indicate that a model can achieve high OBDM scores while still falling short in this more challenging task. To address this limitation, we propose an alternative benchmark that integrates both next-word prediction and semantic representation, and we show that this benchmark provides a more accurate reflection of a model's true language capabilities.

We've conducted a study on periodic and continuous changes in brightness temperatures at quasi-periodic sources associated with solar flares. By analyzing data from the Broadband Absolute Radiometer at 1.5 GHz, we've identified various flaring events and focused on a particularly intense one occurring on August 29, 2014. This flare displayed multiple peaks, with notable periodic features in brightness temperatures observed across different time scales. By examining the changes in brightness temperatures, we've identified a pattern of periodic variations lasting around 10 minutes, accompanied by longer duration fluctuations of up to 2 hours. This pattern is similar to the behavior of coronal seismology models, suggesting that the changes in brightness temperatures are caused by wave-like movements in the corona.

Convolutional processes are widely used in image analysis, but existing time series analysis methods are often inadequate for their spatial or cyclical properties. This study proposes a new method for detecting anomalies in images based on the features generated by convolutional processes. The proposed approach combines statistical analysis with spatial or cyclical weighted local polynomial regression. The method includes selecting the number of relevant terms and assessing the significance of the identified anomalies. Under specific conditions, the proposed procedure is statistically valid and can be theoretically evaluated for the accuracy of anomaly detection. The proposed method's effectiveness is demonstrated through both simulated data and real-world examples, such as detecting defects in materials and analyzing images of sunspots for anomalies.

For specific types of equations known as the dispersion-generalized Kadomtsev-Petviashvili I equations, we have demonstrated that certain mathematical methods cannot be used to find solutions due to the nature of the equations. This lack of convergence is attributed to the presence of 'disturbances' within the mathematical framework. Notably, these equations have been studied in the context of a plasma in the presence of magnetic fields, with implications that solutions may not be computable using standard numerical methods.

In open quantum systems, Kramers' degeneracy can be broken due to the loss of energy to the environment, resulting in a degeneracy lift. This effect is examined in a two-level system interacting with a bosonic bath, where the influence of dissipation on the lift is analyzed. Research indicates that the degeneracy is restored when the system is in thermal equilibrium, whereas it is broken when it deviates from a thermal state, which is typically the case when it is in contact with a low-temperature bath. This degeneracy lift can be utilized to diagnose a non-thermal state of the bath.

This research introduces a novel 3-D neural network-based technique for real-time CSI prediction in OFDM systems, utilizing an unsupervised learning approach. By leveraging an autoencoder, the proposed method enables end-to-end training without reference labels. By predicting both real and imaginary parts of CSI using two separate autoencoders, the method's accuracy is enhanced. Additionally, the model's ability to adapt to changing channel conditions is improved through an extended autoencoder variant that uses previously stored CSI samples as input. This technique's effectiveness is demonstrated through comprehensive simulations, resulting in a significant reduction in CSI errors.

This study examines the application of Gini, Atkinson, and Theil indexes in spatial contexts, where geographical relationships play a crucial role. The variation in these indexes can be understood through the spatial nature of the data, with one index placing more emphasis on the overall income, and the other two placing greater emphasis on income disparities. The Gini index is found to be more sensitive to data aggregation levels than the other two, and a method for adjusting this is presented. The study also explores the spatial dimensions of these indexes and proposes a method for measuring spatial inequality within a region, as well as for detecting clusters of high and low inequality within a network.

We examine the tempered spectral projection kernel given by $P_{\chi, \lambda}(z,w) = \sum_{\lambda \in \chi} \frac{\chi(\lambda^{-1})\lambda^{-1}}{|\lambda|^\chi} \phi_z^\lambda$, where the sum is taken over the integers in a character $\chi$ of a finite group, and consider a unitary character $\chi$ of a finite group. We then investigate the function $P_{\chi, \lambda}(z,w)$ in terms of the Laplace eigenfunctions $\phi_z^\lambda$ of a given cocompact discrete group acting on a Riemannian manifold. Our analysis focuses on the long-time asymptotics of $P_{\chi, \lambda}(z,w)$ as $z$ and $w$ approach infinity, and provides a comparison with the classical case of the Poisson kernel.

A new and efficient method for generating original graphs from their line graphs is presented in the form of MARINLINGA. This algorithm is capable of producing original graphs with specified numbers of vertices and edges, as well as edge-degree sequences that correspond to their line graphs. MARINLINGA's ability to create regular graphs is also demonstrated, outperforming existing approaches by not requiring edge reduction. Furthermore, MARINLINGA's performance is evaluated using edge impurity and average edge difference metrics, showcasing its superiority over other line graph generation algorithms.

Lee-Lee's suggested hypothesis for punctured discs is a broad, flexible concept. It's believed to be a straightforward principle, but when applied to specific subdomains within the realm of real analytic functions, it becomes a powerful tool. The conjecture serves as a foundation for a significant theorem by Adolphson-Sarkisov that describes the geometry of fibrations in a mathematical context.

In this study, we examined the prevalence of dependency bloat in software projects and its long-term impact on dependencies. Our analysis involved a comprehensive examination of 1,334 large-scale Java projects, covering 12,275 versions. The results showed that approximately 32% of direct dependencies are bloated, and this rate remains relatively stable across subsequent project versions. The study also revealed that 81% of indirect dependencies resulting from removal of bloated dependencies in a project's dependencies themselves are also bloated, and more than half of these indirections persist across two levels. These findings underscore the need for innovative solutions to address dependency bloat and promote maintainability of software systems.

The study of interconnected systems has gained significant attention due to their complex behavior resulting from interactions among individual components. This research explores the impact of interconnected systems on the field of polymer science, specifically examining how interconnected polymer systems can be controlled. A one-way control method was previously established, allowing for the separation of polymers based on their unique energy states. This control method was then applied to various types of polymer pairs, with the results indicating a direct correlation between the pair's energy states and control effectiveness. A new study investigates the one-way control method using entangled bi-photons, challenging the traditional understanding of cause-and-effect relationships. According to the study, the control method works in reverse, with the outcome influencing the input, similar to the concept of backward causation. A novel control method utilizing entangled bi-photons was then proposed, with the goal of creating a more efficient and accurate separation process for interconnected polymer systems.

We propose a novel, data-driven approach to assess the most critical scenarios in multistage distributionally robust optimization problems. Our method builds on the scenario root cause analysis concept, adapting it to optimization problems with multiple stages, where we leverage a bilevel two-stage linear programming formulation to identify critical scenarios. Through a simplified yet effective analysis, our approach enables the identification of scenarios that have the greatest impact on the original problem solution. We demonstrate the practical application of our method through a case study in hydrothermal generation systems.

Recent studies have demonstrated that incorporating spatial and temporal information into action anticipation models can yield better results. However, these approaches often neglect the potential benefits of using kernel-based methods to capture complex relationships between pixels and semantic features. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that seamlessly integrates spatial, temporal, and semantic features using a combination of convolutional and radial basis function kernels. To further enhance performance, we also introduce a novel loss function that encourages the network to generate multiple, diverse feature representations. Experimental results on UCF101-HABO W and EPIC-KITCHENS-HAB show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art models, and that incorporating radial basis function kernels specifically yields a significant gain in performance over traditional spatial and temporal kernels.

We investigate the behavior of local properties in a complex system undergoing two distinct thermalization processes, regular thermalization and deep thermalization. Our analysis reveals that while both processes result in similar thermalization effects, regular thermalization leaves a trace of the initial state's influence on a specific observable, in contrast to deep thermalization, which completely erases this influence, leaving no remainder in the observable's response function. Using the Ising model as a test case, we demonstrate that deep thermalization is a more efficient process than regular thermalization, especially at low temperatures. Furthermore, we show that the Ising model exhibits deep thermalization as a result of quenching the transverse field to zero, a scenario that can be explained by the loss of memory in the local properties.

We establish connections between the theories of nuclear operators and pseudo-differential operators, and specifically, derive criteria for nuclear pseudo-differential operators that are applicable to various types of function spaces, including those that are not necessarily Banach spaces. These criteria are then applied to specific instances, including nuclear Schrödinger operators and their associated time-dependent problems. Additionally, the notion of nuclearity is linked to the Riesz transforms within the context of Calderón-Zygmund theory.

The 5G rollout is being hindered by the presence of obstructions in urban landscapes, which hinder signal strength. We investigate exposure to 5G base station radiation in areas with both open and blocked sightlines, leveraging a comparative framework to assess exposure levels under different scenarios. By employing a spatial analysis tool, our study examines exposure levels within a given radius around each base station, both in unobstructed and obstructed conditions, to determine the impact of obstructions on overall exposure levels. The results of our analysis, which took into consideration various types of obstructions and a range of base station heights, indicate that the Line-of-Sight condition tends to increase exposure to electromagnetic fields, particularly at greater distances.

Deep learning models have been enhanced by the use of CODEs to improve their out-of-distribution detection and classification capabilities. These strategies have been shown to improve performance in model-based anomaly detection but have not yet been applied in the context of anomaly detection through the analysis of data characteristics. This study proposes a CODE framework for anomaly detection through the examination of the latent space created by the data. By utilizing a CODE, we can effectively distinguish between normal and anomalous data points, even when the data is generated from a complex, non-linear distribution. This is the first instance of applying CODEs to characterize data in a non-anomalous context. Our results demonstrate that the proposed CODE can effectively distinguish between normal and anomalous data points, even when the data is generated from a complex, non-linear distribution.

Recent advancements in the resummation of jet distributions have led to significant progress in the field. Our study presents the first numerical results of next-to-leading-order calculations for the dijet momentum distribution in hadron collisions, taking into account the impact of initial-state effects up to next-to-leading order. This calculation is further enhanced by incorporating both next-to-next-to-leading-order corrections to the parton shower and leading-order corrections to initial-state radiations. Notably, our findings show substantial improvements in the description of jet distributions when using next-to-leading-order calculations, particularly when compared to simulations using NNLO+LO combinations.

Recent breakthroughs in self-supervised learning have enabled the successful use of unlabeled data for training models that can outperform their supervised counterparts in visual recognition tasks. This study focuses on the application of self-supervised learning to a specific visual task - 3D object pose estimation. By utilising a pre-trained model that has been trained on a diverse set of visual data through self-supervised learning, our approach can effectively leverage unlabeled data in 3D object pose estimation tasks. Our experimental results demonstrate that this method can effectively transfer knowledge from diverse visual domains to a specific task, even when the source and target datasets have significant differences in their object distributions. Moreover, our approach can effectively adapt to new objects with minimal additional training.

The RECol framework addresses the challenge of applying transfer learning in outlier detection, which typically relies on a pre-trained neural network trained on image classification tasks. However, outlier detection models often fail to leverage the full potential of transfer learning due to the separate treatment of input features as independent data.
